Start here

🌱In plain words

This guide explains Twigum, a private chat app for families and friends. It is written so that anyone who can read carefully can follow it, even if they have never run a server or written code. Hard ideas come with an everyday comparison first, and then the exact technical details, so experts lose nothing.

Who this guide is for

This guide is for anyone who wants to run their own Twigum server: for a family, a club, a school or a small company. It shows how to install it, set every option, keep it running, update it, back it up and fix problems. It also explains how the app and the server work inside, including the encryption.

It does not describe any particular organisation's servers. The only outside service it mentions is the public Twigum front door at twigum.app, because that is how people find your server and how invite links work (§1.3 and §3.14). Example addresses such as chat.example.com are made up; use your own.

How to read this guide

You do not have to read it in order.

  • New to Twigum? Read §1 (the big picture), then the glossary (§10) whenever a word is unfamiliar.
  • Want a server running today? Go to §7 Run your own server. Every step says where to run it, what to type, what you should see and what to do if it fails.
  • Fixing a problem? Start with §9 Troubleshooting.
  • Curious how it works? Read §2–§6.
  • Looking up a setting? Appendix B lists every setting.

The coloured boxes

🌱In plain words

A short, simple explanation of a hard idea, often with an everyday comparison. Read it first, then the detail after it.

💡Tip

A shortcut or a good habit that saves time.

📘Good To Know

A fact that is easy to miss but matters later.

⚠️Warning

Something risky: it can lose data, lock people out or break the server. Read it twice.

🛠️Step by step

A procedure. Each one tells you where to run it, what it does, the exact command, what you should see, how to check it worked and what to do if it fails.

Commands and where to type them

A command is a line of text you type into a terminal (a window where you type instructions to a computer instead of clicking). Commands in this guide are shown in dark boxes like this:

curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version
  • Type (or paste) the whole line, then press Enter.
  • Text in angle brackets, like <version>, is a placeholder. Replace it, including the brackets, with your own value.
  • sudo at the start means "run this as the administrator of this computer". It asks for your password. The password does not show while you type; that is normal.
  • # starts a comment in shell commands. Everything after it is a note for you and is ignored by the computer.
📘Good To Know: Which shell?

A shell is the program inside the terminal that reads your commands. All server commands in this guide are for bash, the standard shell on Debian, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS. If your own computer uses another shell (zsh, fish), log in to the server first (for example with ssh) and type the commands there.

What "the code says" means here

Everything in this guide was checked against the Twigum source code at version 26.11.1401 (source commit 2da30e8f). When the guide says where something is in the code, it writes the file and line, like web/server.py:4708. You never need to open these files to follow the guide. They are there so that a developer can check the claim, and because line numbers can move a little in later versions, search for the function name if a line does not match.

  • Code wins. When a README or a code comment disagrees with what the code actually does, this guide follows the code.

  • Unverified marks something that could not be checked from the code or with a safe read-only test. Treat it as "probably right, check before relying on it".

  • No passwords, private keys, tokens or other secrets appear in this guide.

Version numbers

Twigum versions look like 26.11.1401: two-digit year (26 = 2026), two-digit month (11 = November), then DDRR: the two-digit day (14) and that day's release number starting at 01. So 26.11.1401 is the first release made on 14 November 2026, and the first release on 1 January 2027 would be 27.01.0101.

The native apps also have a build number that must always go up: the full date plus the release number, YYYYMMDDRR, for example 2026111401.

1. Twigum in plain words

1.1 What Twigum is

🌱In plain words

Imagine a post office that only your family uses. Everyone writes letters, puts each one in a locked box, and only the people it is meant for have a key that opens it. The post office stores and delivers the boxes, but it does not hold the keys, so it cannot read the letters. Twigum works like that. The server is the post office, the app on each phone or computer writes and locks the letters, and the keys stay on people's devices.

Twigum is a private chat app for family and friends (its tagline, on web/static/og-twigum.jpg, is "Private chat for family and friends"). People send messages, photos, videos and files, one-to-one or in groups. Messages and files are encrypted (scrambled so only the right devices can unscramble them) on the sender's device before they leave it (§5).

It is source-available (anyone can read the code, under the Twigum License 2.0, LICENSE.md) and self-hostable: each family or organisation can run its own server. A shared public front door at twigum.app helps people find their organisation's server and sign in to it.

⚠️Warning: Don't over-promise the encryption

Do not describe Twigum as "end-to-end encrypted against the server operator" without the exceptions. The project's own README.md:3 and the correction notice in web/patch-notes.html:25 withdrew that claim for accounts that once had an older (v1) key backup. The full list of what the server can and cannot see is in §5.8.

The four big ideas:

  1. One server, one web app. Each server is a single Python program. It sends the app's pages to the browser and answers the app's questions (the API) from the same address. (web/server.py)
  2. The device does the locking. Messages and files are encrypted on the device with the browser's built-in cryptography (WebCrypto, web/static/crypto.js). The server stores only scrambled text (ciphertext) and, for each device that should read a message, a wrap: a copy of the message's key locked so only that one device can open it. The server is not given the keys for direct messages, group messages or files. Exceptions: the public Lobby on public-mode servers, and accounts with a legacy v1 key backup (§5.6, §5.8). A server that sends people modified app code is not defended against (§5.8).
  3. The phone and desktop apps are thin wrappers. iPhone/iPad, Android and desktop apps all show the same web app inside a built-in browser window (a WebView) and add phone features: notifications, the share sheet, saving files, switching servers. (ios/, android/, desktop/)
  4. No always-open connection. The app asks the server "anything new?" and the server holds the question open until something changes (long-polling, GET /api/wait), then the app fetches only what changed (GET /api/sync). (§3.5)

1.2 Where Twigum runs (platforms)

Platform How it runs Code Notes
Web browser / PWA Any modern browser. Can be "installed" as an app (a PWA, progressive web app) via web/manifest.webmanifest and the service worker web/sw.js web/ The main app. Every other platform shows this one.
iPhone / iPad Swift app with a built-in browser window (WKWebView) ios/ Bundle ID app.branchchat.ios. Three parts: the app, a Notification Service extension and a Share extension. iOS 16.0 or newer.
Android Java app with the system WebView android/ Package app.branchchat.android, Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer, targets API 36.
Linux desktop Electron app desktop/ AppImage, deb, rpm and tar.gz for x86_64 and arm64; Flatpak manifest in desktop/flatpak/.
Windows desktop Electron app desktop/ nsis and msi installers (plus a dist:win:arm64 nsis script).
macOS No native Mac target in the code. desktop/package.json has a dist:mac script, but desktop/BUILD.md:30-32 says it has never been built or tested. —
Apple Watch No watch app. The watch only mirrors the iPhone's notifications (web/server.py:8166). —
📘Good To Know: Why "branchchat" keeps appearing

Twigum used to be called BranchChat, and its code name is huzz-chat. Many internal names keep the old spelling on purpose (for example the iOS bundle ID app.branchchat.ios and the cookie huzz_chat_session). Renaming them would break app updates, saved keys and decryption. Use only the name Twigum in anything people read. The full list is under Twigum in the glossary (§10).

1.3 The servers

🌱In plain words

A server is a computer that is always on and connected to the internet, waiting for apps to ask it things. Each family or group can have its own Twigum server, like each town having its own post office. The front door is like a shared information desk that tells you which post office is yours.

There are two kinds of server in this guide:

Kind Example address What it is for
Your server https://chat.example.com Where your people's accounts, locked messages and files live. You run it. Everything in §7 is about this one.
The public front door https://twigum.app Run by the Twigum project. It hosts the sign-in page where people type or pick a server, the directory of servers that chose to be listed, and the landing page that invite links open. It never sees your people's passwords or messages (§3.14).

Your server works on its own. Two things connect it to the front door:

  • Invite links open through twigum.app/join?... by default, whether or not your server is listed (since 26.10.10, web/directory.py invite_link). The secret part of the link stays in the person's browser and is never sent to twigum.app. Set BC_INVITE_DIRECT=1 if you want plain https://<your server>/welcome#t=... links instead (§3.14).
  • Being listed in the public directory is optional and off by default (BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=0). Turn it on if you want people to be able to find your server by name (§3.14, §7.9).

The front door in detail. A front door is a Twigum server started with BC_HOME_MODE=1 (web/directory.py). Its special sign-in page (BC_FRONTDOOR) turns on automatically when open sign-up (or public mode) and home mode are both on, unless set by hand (web/frontdoor.py:29-30). It shows a sign-in page with a box for a server address, the organisation directory (/directory, /api/directory) and the pages that invite links land on.

The default invite link looks like this:

https://twigum.app/join?s=<server host>&n=<server name>&k=<key fingerprint>#t=<invite token>
  • s is your server's address, n its display name, k the start of its identity key fingerprint (a short code that proves the server is the real one, §3.14).
  • Everything after # (the fragment) stays in the browser and is never sent to any server. That is where the secret invite token lives.
  • A direct https://<your server>/welcome#t=<token> link is used instead only by the front door's own server, when BC_INVITE_DIRECT=1, or on http test installs (web/directory.py:56,328-339).

1.4 How an app chooses a server (the server picker)

🌱In plain words

When you open the app for the first time it does not know which post office is yours. It starts at the shared information desk (the front door). You type your server's address, pick it from a list, or tap an invite link. The app checks that the address really is a Twigum server and then remembers it, so next time it goes straight there.

Step by step:

  1. Open the front door. Web: https://twigum.app/. Android: built-in branchchatServerUrl=https://twigum.app/ (android/gradle.properties). Desktop: DEFAULT_SERVER = 'https://twigum.app/' (desktop/main.js:15). iPhone/iPad: TwigumServerURL = https://branchchat.app/ (ios/Twigum/Info.plist, same fallback in AppConfig.defaultServerURL).
  2. Choose a server. Type an address, pick one from the directory, or follow an invite link.
  3. The app checks the server before trusting it:
    • iPhone/iPad never probes. Add server loads the front door's /#own page (WebViewController.swift:522-525). A server is remembered only when the page reaches a host that the front door's /api/directory or /api/signin-servers lists, with the exact host on port 443 (WebViewController.swift:330-332). Internationalised (punycode) names and other ports are refused. Up to 50 servers (maxKnown).
    • Android (ServerConfig.probe, ServerConfig.java:272-274): must be https with a valid certificate and no redirects, and one of /.well-known/branchchat, /api/version or /api/health must answer like a Twigum server.
    • Desktop (desktop/main.js, desktop/servers-model.js): /.well-known/branchchat or /api/version, else /api/health must return {"ok": true}. Hand-offs from the front door must be https. A server added by hand may use plain http only for *.home, *.local, *.lan, *.internal, localhost, or private and loopback addresses (10/8, 172.16–31, 192.168/16, 127/8) (desktop/main.js:61-62).
  4. The app remembers it and reopens it next time (iPhone: bc.servers.session in the Keychain; Android since 26.10.6; desktop: servers.json). Every app has a Servers menu to switch, add, rename or remove servers (§6).
⚠️Warning: Why the iPhone app still opens branchchat.app

The iPhone app's front door is https://branchchat.app/ on purpose. The comment calls it TEMPORARY (Info.plist:30-35, AppConfig.swift:16-17). Browsers keep cookies and stored keys per address, so moving the iPhone app to twigum.app before the planned branchchat.app → twigum.app hand-off exists would make every iPhone user lose their sign-in and their keys (docs/TWIGUM-DOMAIN-CUTOVER.md:9-16). Do not "fix" it.

How a server describes itself. Every server answers GET /.well-known/branchchat with a small card about itself. Real example from the public front door:

{"branchchat": 2, "name": "Twigum", "login_url": "https://branchchat.app/", "version": "26.11.1007",
 "identity_key": "...", "key_fp": "...", "icon": "/directory-icon",
 "invites": {"check": "/api/invite/check", "welcome": "/welcome"}}

identity_key is the server's public directory identity key (kept in server-identity.json, web/directory.py). Public means it is safe to share; the matching private key never leaves the server.

💡Tip: Try it yourself

You can look at any server's card. In a terminal type curl -s https://twigum.app/.well-known/branchchat and press Enter. You should see one line of text like the example above. curl is a small program that fetches a web address and prints what comes back.

2. How the pieces fit together (architecture)

🌱In plain words

Architecture means "which parts there are and how they talk to each other", like a map of a town that shows the houses, the roads and the post office. Twigum has three main parts: the apps (on phones and computers), the server (the post office) and a few outside services the server uses to send notifications and emails.

2.1 The parts and the outside services

Read the figure from left to right:

  1. People use one of four kinds of app. All of them are the same web app inside.
  2. Every app talks only to its Twigum server, using HTTPS (the locked, private version of the web's language; the padlock in a browser).
  3. The server is one Python program. It keeps everything in ordinary files in one folder, the state directory (§3.3).
  4. The server talks to outside services only for these jobs:
    • Web Push services (run by browser makers such as Google, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft) to wake browsers when a message arrives. The server sends only a locked "wake up" note, never the message (§3.9).
    • Apple Push Notification service (APNs) to wake the iPhone/iPad app (§3.9).
    • Email (an SMTP mail server or the computer's own sendmail) for sign-in codes, invites and password resets.
    • The front door directory at twigum.app, only if the server is set to be listed (§3.14).
    • KLIPY, a GIF search service, through the server so that the app never contacts KLIPY directly (/api/gifs).
📘Good To Know: Android gets no push service

The Android app does not use Google's push service (FCM). Instead it keeps its own quiet connection to the server open in the background and checks for new messages itself (§6.2). That is why the Android app shows a small, silent "Sync" notification.

What sits in front of your server. The Twigum server itself speaks plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:8766 by default and expects something in front of it to add HTTPS: a Cloudflare Tunnel, the Caddy web server, or your own reverse proxy (§7.4). The installer can set up the first two for you.

2.2 What is in the code (repository layout)

🌱In plain words

The repository (or repo) is the folder that holds all of Twigum's code and its history, like a big binder with every page ever written and a note of who changed what. You only need it to build the apps or run a server from source.

Path What it holds
VERSION The single version string for the server and all apps (26.11.1401).
web/ The server and the web app. server.py (10,232 lines) is the HTTP server. The other *.py files are server modules (below). HTML pages, sw.js, manifest.webmanifest and static/ (JS, CSS, images, vendor WASM) are the app. web/tests/ holds 185 test files.
web/static/app.js The main app code (25,214 lines, about 1,100 functions).
web/static/crypto.js All of the app's cryptography (WebCrypto).
server/ The self-hosting kit: install.sh, branch-chat.service (a locked-down systemd unit), config.env.example, docker-compose.yml, backup.sh, requirements.txt, server/tests/.
Dockerfile The container image recipe (python:3.13-slim).
ios/, android/, desktop/ The native apps (§6).
crates/vodozemac-js/ Rust → WASM build of vodozemac (Olm/Megolm) for the web (§5.5).
scripts/vodo-cutover.py Operator script for the vodozemac switch-over (§5.5).
tools/ Release and packaging tools, including make-server-release.sh (builds the server packages, §7.2).
tests/ run-all.sh plus version-comparator tests.
docs/ Design notes and guides: self-hosting.md, server/*.md (one guide per platform), DIRECTORY.md, INVITES.md, public-mode.md, VERSIONING.md and brand assets.
DESIGN-crypto-hardening.md Design of signing, device trust and key backup v2.

Server modules (web/*.py)

A module is one file of code with one job. The server is split like this:

Module Responsibility
server.py HTTP handler (Handler), routing (Handler.dispatch), messages, sync, devices, uploads, groups, lobby, sessions, startup (main).
bcconfig.py Configuration loading (env > config file > default), host list, version, URLs.
accounts.py Accounts, password hashing (scrypt), invites, sessions store helpers.
adminpage.py Server Administrator page and /api/server-admin/*; settings schema (91 settings, web/adminpage.py:79-239) and Apply.
publicmode.py Public-server features: sign-up, Turnstile, blocking/reporting, Lobby content filter, moderation.
directory.py Directory reporting to/from the front door, /.well-known/branchchat, LAN admin listener.
frontdoor.py Front-door pages.
device_sig.py Server-side verification of device and message signatures (mirrors crypto.js).
device_approval.py Approve-a-new-device flow (flag BC_DEVICE_APPROVAL).
device_names.py Device and sign-in naming.
webpush.py Web Push (VAPID, payload encryption, send via curl).
apnspush.py Apple push (APNs) for the iOS app.
dmwebhook.py, memberwebhook.py Admin-configured webhooks.
bugreports.py In-app bug reports.
welcomebot.py, welcomebot_content.py Optional welcome bot ("Twigum Helper").
contentfilter.py Lobby text filter (used by publicmode).
vodozemac_proto.py Olm/Megolm server helpers (flag BC_VODOZEMAC).
unfurl.py Link previews.
downloads.py /download/* app downloads.
legalpage.py /license* pages.
featuremail.py "Feature news" email opt-out.
mailtemplates.py Email templates.
manage.py CLI: health check, user management.
trim_sessions.py, twigum_redirect.py Maintenance and redirect helpers.

2.3 Inside the app and the server (components)

In plain words:

  • app.js is the app's brain: it draws the screens, keeps in sync with the server and handles sending.
  • crypto.js is the locksmith: it makes keys, locks and unlocks messages and checks signatures.
  • vodozemac is an optional second locksmith for a newer kind of lock (Megolm), off by default (§5.5).
  • sw.js (the service worker) is a helper that runs in the background, even when the page is closed. It keeps a copy of the app for offline use and shows notifications.
  • IndexedDB is a small database inside the browser that keeps the device's keys and a locked copy of recent messages.
  • On the server, Handler.dispatch is the receptionist: it looks at each request and passes it to the right desk (sign-in, messages, devices, files, admin, public mode, directory).

3. The server, inside

🌱In plain words

The server is one program that runs all the time. It does four jobs: it hands out the app (the web pages and code), it checks who people are (sign-in), it stores and passes on locked messages and files, and it wakes up devices when something new arrives. It keeps everything in ordinary files in one folder instead of a big database, which makes it simple to back up: copy the folder and you have everything.

3.1 What it is built with (stack)

A stack is the list of tools a program is built from.

Item Value Source
Language Python 3 (container uses python:3.13-slim) Dockerfile
HTTP server Standard library http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer with BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass Handler; protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1", server_version = "huzz-chat", TCP_NODELAY on web/server.py class Handler (line 4197), main() (line 10150)
Framework None. Routing is a long if/elif chain in Handler.dispatch (line 4723). web/server.py
Dependencies cryptography>=42,<47 only (Web Push VAPID/payload encryption, APNs ES256 JWT signing in web/apnspush.py, P-256 signature checks, Lobby re-seal). brotli optional for static compression. server/requirements.txt, web/server.py (import brotli in try)
Database None. JSON files plus an append-only messages.jsonl in STATE_DIR (§3.3). web/server.py
Real-time HTTP long-poll /api/wait + /api/sync. No WebSockets. §3.5
Outbound HTTP for push curl subprocess (HTTP/2) web/webpush.py, web/apnspush.py; Dockerfile installs curl
Default bind BC_HOST=127.0.0.1, BC_PORT=8766 (container: 0.0.0.0:8766) web/bcconfig.py, Dockerfile
📘Good To Know: Why no database and no framework?

Most web servers use a database program (like PostgreSQL) and a framework (like Django). Twigum uses neither. The whole server is the Python standard library plus one extra package, cryptography. Fewer moving parts means fewer things to install, update and secure, and a backup is just a copy of one folder (§7.11).

3.2 How the server starts and runs

There is one process (one running copy of the program). It serves the HTML pages, the static files and the API.

What happens at start-up (web/server.py main()):

  1. migrate_state() reads STATE_DIR/SCHEMA_VERSION. If it is older than the code's SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 1), it first copies the state to pre-migrate-<ver>-<time> and then runs the steps in MIGRATIONS (currently empty: MIGRATIONS = {}). In plain words: if the data was saved by an older version, make a safety copy and then convert it.
  2. readmarks_prune(), migrate_sessions_once() (writes session-migrate-30d.done), load_messages() (reads messages.jsonl into memory).
  3. Background threads (small helpers that run side by side): the log flusher and the presence ticker.
  4. load_groups(), load_glinks(), sweep_old() (deletes unfinished uploads and unclaimed files older than one day; it runs once at start only, there is no periodic sweep, web/server.py:10174 is its only caller), then the key-backup expiry thread (web/server.py:10170-10175).
  5. welcomebot.init, device_approval.init, featuremail.init, adminpage.init.
  6. Start the web server (ThreadingHTTPServer); directory.start_reporter() (signed "I'm alive" pings to the front door, only when BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=1, §3.14); directory.start_admin_listener() (a separate home-network-only admin listener; see docs/DIRECTORY-ADMIN-API.md).
  7. If the server fails to start after someone pressed Apply on the Administrator page, adminpage.recover_after_failed_start puts the previous settings back.
💡Tip: Restarting cleans up

Because sweep_old runs only at start-up, a restart is also the moment old unfinished uploads are cleared. Any update restarts the server, so this normally happens on its own.

The two ways to run it. A systemd service is a program that the Linux system starts at boot and restarts if it crashes. A Docker container is a sealed box with the program and everything it needs inside, so it runs the same everywhere.

Way What runs it Code Data (STATE_DIR) Settings
Native (installer default) systemd service branch-chat from server/branch-chat.service: runs as the locked-down user branchchat, with BC_CONFIG=/etc/branch-chat/config.env, BC_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/branch-chat, BC_APP_DIR=/opt/branch-chat/app and systemd sandboxing /opt/branch-chat/app (a link to the newest folder in /opt/branch-chat/releases/) /var/lib/branch-chat /etc/branch-chat/config.env
Docker server/docker-compose.yml, service branch-chat: image built from Dockerfile (python:3.13-slim, user id 10001, read-only, all extra powers dropped, HEALTHCHECK runs manage.py healthcheck) inside the image (/app) the /data volume (./data next to the compose file by default) config.env next to the compose file

Health checks. A health check is a tiny question that proves the server is up.

Ask Answer when healthy Notes
GET /healthz ok (plain text) Answered before the host check (Handler, line ~4705), so it works on any address. manage.py healthcheck uses it.
GET /api/health {"ok": true}
GET /api/version the version JSON, for example {"version":"26.11.1401","api":"26.11","min_app":"26.11.0",...} api is the year and month (YY.MM); min_app is the oldest app version allowed.
🛠️Step by step: Check that a server is up

Where: any computer with a terminal (bash).

What it does: asks the server for its version without signing in. It changes nothing.

  1. Type:

    curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version

    (Use your server's address instead of chat.example.com.)

  2. You should see one line starting with {"version":"26.11. and ending with }.

  3. It worked if the version is the one you expect.
  4. If it fails:
    • Nothing comes back, or "Could not resolve host": the address is wrong or the server's name is not set up (DNS). Check the spelling.
    • A web page full of HTML (a Cloudflare or proxy error page, or "502"): the front part (tunnel or proxy) is up but the Twigum program is not answering. See §9.
    • {"error": "That page was not found."}: the server is running but does not know this address. Add it to BC_HOSTS or fix BC_PUBLIC_URL (Appendix B).

The path of one request (request pipeline)

🌱In plain words

Every time the app asks the server something, the question goes through a row of checkpoints, like going through security at an airport. If any checkpoint says no, the question is turned away with a short message, and the rest of the server never sees it.

  1. Read the body (only for POST, PUT and DELETE, which carry data). If the data cannot be read: 400 "That request was not accepted."
  2. Cross-site guard (post_guard_ok, only for /api/*): checks that the request came from the Twigum page itself (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site headers and the content type). If not: 403. This stops other websites from tricking a signed-in browser into sending messages (CSRF).
  3. /healthz is answered straight away with ok.
  4. Host check (host_ok): is the address the request was sent to one of this server's names (HOSTS)? If not: 404 {"error": "That page was not found."}.
  5. HTTPS redirect: if the server's public address is https and a trusted proxy says the request came in over plain http, answer 308 and send the browser to the https address.
  6. Handler.dispatch finds the right handler. Public pages (sign-in, version, static files) are answered without a session. Everything else needs a valid session cookie (self.require), or the answer is 401.

Code: web/server.py:4450-4526, 4703-4710.

3.3 Where data is kept (storage)

🌱In plain words

Everything the server knows lives in one folder, the state directory (STATE_DIR). Inside are plain text files, each holding one kind of thing: one for accounts, one for sign-ins, one long list of locked messages, folders of locked file pieces and so on. When the server changes a file it writes a new copy and then swaps it in, all at once, so a crash can never leave a half-written file.

All state lives under STATE_DIR (BC_STATE_DIR, default /var/lib/huzz-chat in web/bcconfig.py; /data in Docker). Writes use a process-wide lock (_store_lock) and atomic file replace. Files (names collected from os.path.join(STATE_DIR, ...) in web/*.py):

File / dir Contents Written by

sessions.json Authoritative session rows (id, user, expiry, bound device, user agent, name) accounts.py, server.py
session.key HMAC key used to sign session cookies (secret; never logged) server.py
messages.jsonl Append-only log of message rows (ciphertext + metadata; see Message row below). Loaded into memory at start. append_message

Message row. Each line of messages.jsonl is one JSON object. Fields set by the server in Handler.post_message (line 8029): seq (monotonic integer), id (32 hex chars = 16 random bytes), sender, ts, box (dm, group or lobby), conversation fields (a/b for DMs, g for groups), plus the client-provided ciphertext fields: iv, ct (text, max 48,000 chars, TEXT_CT_MAX), wraps (per-device wrapped message keys) or epoch / epoch_iv / epoch_ct (group/Lobby), optional blob ({id, chunks, bytes, …}, web/server.py:8117-8122, 9239-9251), signature fields (sig, sender_device, ctr; sd is only the field name inside the APNs payload), sender_name (set by the server, line 8115), and for Megolm alg: "megolm", session_id, message_index, body. Deleted messages keep a tombstone row ("The row stays so clients can show that it was removed. Ciphertext and the encrypted file are erased." — delete_message).

Limits (web/server.py constants, lines ~244–300):

Constant Value Meaning
PLAIN_MAX BC_FILE_MAX_MB MiB (default 2048, clamped 1–4096) Max plaintext file size
ORIGINAL_MAX min(PLAIN_MAX, 1 GiB) Over this the client must send HD/SD instead of the original (enforced by the client)
CHUNK 8 MiB Upload/download chunk (plaintext)
PART_MAX CHUNK + 64 KiB Max encrypted part body
JSON_MAX 96 KiB Max JSON body

Posting rate 1 message per second per account (too_fast, 429)

File retention (there is no time-based expiry for shared files in the code):

What When it is removed Evidence
Files attached to messages (photos, videos, other files) No time limit. Removed only when the message is deleted (delete_message, web/server.py:8275-8276) or the account is fully deleted (web/static/public.js:559)
Videos only evict_old_videos removes the oldest claimed videos when the storage budget or free disk runs short. Readers then get 410 {expired: true} and see "This video expired to free space." Photos and other files are never evicted. web/server.py:2325-2366, 9500; app.js:12328

Invites / group links 14-day and 30-day timers apply to invites and group links only web/accounts.py:1278 (GONE_KEEP), web/server.py:1948

There is no cleanup cron; server/install.sh:448-478 only adds a nightly backup timer. A "96-hour expiry for shared files" was mentioned during review but does not exist in the code (Q24).

⚠️Warning: Keep the state directory private

Several files in it are secrets: session.key (lets anyone forge sign-ins), vapid.json, server-identity.json (the private half of the server's directory identity), welcome-bot-key.json and klipy.key. The installer creates the folder with mode 700 (only the server's own user can open it). Do not loosen that, and keep backups just as private (§7.11).

3.4 What the server answers (API reference)

🌱In plain words

An API (application programming interface) is the list of questions a program will answer, and how to ask them. Each question has a method (GET means "give me", POST means "here is something, act on it") and a path (like /api/messages). The app only ever talks to the server through these. You never need to call them by hand, but they are listed here so a developer can find where each feature lives.

All endpoints return JSON unless noted. Errors are {"error": "<sentence for people>"} with an HTTP status. "Auth" means a valid session cookie (Handler.require, line 4439). The table order follows Handler.dispatch.

📘Good To Know: Error messages are written for people

Every error comes back as {"error": "<one sentence a person can understand>"} with an HTTP status number, for example 401 (not signed in), 403 (not allowed), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 422 (cannot be processed) and 429 (too many, slow down).

3.4.5 How the app hears about changes ("events")

There are no WebSocket events. Clients learn about changes by:

  1. GET /api/wait?cv=<n>&t=<s> — blocks until the server's change version differs from cv (or a read-mark wake for this account), up to t seconds (max 25; capped at 7 s while anyone is typing). Returns {"ok": true, "cv": <n>, "changed": <bool>}. It holds no store lock while waiting. (web/server.py ~6432)
  2. GET /api/sync?since=<seq>&... — returns everything that changed. The "event types" are the fields in the sync response:
Sync field Meaning
me username, role, owner, expires_in, key_backup, totp, key_backup_reset, key_backup_v, key_backup_mode
messages, more New rows after since (max 100), and whether more are waiting
removed, gone, edited, edit removed = ids deleted since the client's gone cursor; gone = the new gone cursor; edited = edited rows; edit = the new edit cursor (web/server.py:6493-6505, 6700-6703)
reactions, reactions_rev Reactions (sent when the revision changed)
typing Who is typing where
online Presence
friends, incoming, outgoing Friends and requests
devices Device public keys and signing fields for people you talk to (names only for your own)
lobby, groups Membership, epochs and wraps
pins, receipts, my_seen, read fields Pins, receipts, read state
mutes, chatlist Per-account chat settings
display_names, name_colors, contacts, nicknames, avatars Profile data
admin_approval, device_approvals, device_notices Pending approvals and "new device added" notices
file_max, original_max, cv Limits, change version
public Public-mode extra data from publicmode.sync_extra(), present only when public features are on (web/server.py:6737-6738)
crypto_v, vodo_identities, vodo_todevice Only with BC_VODOZEMAC=1; vodo_todevice only when the client passes todevice=1 (so native notifiers do not consume the queue)
st, same Delta stamp. same: true means the people/keys/groups fields (SYNC_DELTA_KEYS) were left out because they are unchanged; messages and the other fields are still sent (web/server.py:330-332, 6779-6787)

The client's syncUrl() (web/static/app.js line 2805) builds the query (since, react, gone, edit, st, todevice=1). The session cookie is refreshed in the sync response when it is close to expiry.

3.4.6 What the server checks when a message is sent

🌱In plain words

When the app sends a message, the server checks it like a careful clerk: Is it the right shape and size? Is it signed? Is the sender allowed to write to this chat? Was it already sent (a double tap)? Is the sender going too fast? Only then does it store the message and wake up the people it is for.

Handler.post_message (line 8029), in order:

  1. Validate JSON shape and sizes.
  2. _refuse_unsigned_when_listed: a classic (non-Megolm) message without a signature, from a device that has published a signing key, gets 422 {"sign_required": true, "error": "Reload Twigum to send this message."} (only ctr_reused replies carry a state field; web/server.py:8650-8653).
  3. Lobby on a public-mode server: publicmode.lobby_check opens, filters and re-seals the text with the client-supplied ck (§5.8).
  4. Build the row with _dm_row / _group_row / _lobby_row: friendship / membership checks, claim the attached blob, check wraps belong to the right devices, parse Megolm fields.
  5. Client id (cid) de-duplication for 600 s (SHARE_CID_TTL).
  6. Counter check: a reused (sender_device, ctr) gets 422 {"error": "Reload Twigum to send this message.", "state": "ctr_reused", "max_ctr": n} (ctr_reused_reply, web/server.py:1157, 1196-1197). The client retries once automatically (§5.4).
  7. Rate limit: more than one post per second → 429.
  8. Assign seq, id, sender, ts; append_message; bump change version (wakes /api/wait).
  9. Work out push targets (minus muted chats and Do Not Disturb), reply 200, then call webpush.notify, apnspush.notify, dmwebhook.notify.

add_wraps (line 9258) lets a device that holds a key wrap it for a newer device. It applies to DMs only (web/server.py:9273). Signed messages need a signed re-wrap (twigum-rewrap-v1, stored as rewraps, line 9305). wrap_allowed_for_device (web/server.py:3206-3223) blocks old keys for a new device unless another device on the same account cross-signed it; otherwise the device's first_seen must be ≤ the message ts + WRAP_SKEW_SECONDS (120 s).

3.5 How the app stays up to date (sync)

🌱In plain words

Imagine phoning a shop and asking "has my parcel come in?". Instead of saying "no" and hanging up, the shopkeeper says "hold the line" and waits up to 25 seconds. The moment the parcel arrives they say "yes!" and you go and collect it. If nothing comes, they say "not yet" and you ring again. That is long-polling: /api/wait is the "hold the line" call, and /api/sync is collecting the parcel.

The numbered steps in the figure:

  1. When the app starts, it asks for everything since the last row it has (since=<seq>; seq is the running number of each message row).
  2. The server sends the new rows plus a change number (cv), which goes up whenever anything changes on the server.
  3. The app asks /api/wait with that change number.
  4. The server holds the question open until the change number moves, up to 25 seconds (7 seconds while anyone is typing, so typing dots appear quickly). It holds no lock while waiting, so waiting apps never slow the server down.
  5. The server answers whether something changed.
  6. If so, the app asks /api/sync for only the changes.
  7. The server sends them, and the loop starts again at step 3.

At most 100 rows come back per sync (SYNC_LIMIT); more: true means "ask again for the rest". The fields of a sync answer are listed in §3.4.5.

3.6 Signing in and staying signed in

🌱In plain words

Signing in is like showing ID at a door. First you say who you are and give your password. If this browser is new, the server also emails you a 6-digit code, the way a bank texts you a code, so a stolen password alone is not enough. If you turned on two-factor (an authenticator app), you type its code too. Then the server gives your browser a session cookie: a signed wristband that says "this person is signed in" for the next 30 days, so you don't have to sign in every time.

  1. The person types their username and password; the app sends them to POST /api/login.
  2. The server checks the password against the stored scrypt hash (a slow, one-way scramble, so the real password is never stored).
  3. If two-factor is on, the person types the 6-digit code from their authenticator app (POST /api/login/totp).
  4. If this browser already passed an email code (it has the huzz_chat_verified cookie, valid 400 days) and no backup step is needed, the person is signed in now. Otherwise the server emails a 6-digit code (valid 10 minutes, 5 tries, resend after 60 seconds), and the person types it (POST /api/login/code).
  5. If the account has a key backup, the app shows it, the person unlocks it with their recovery key or backup passphrase, and the app finishes with POST /api/login/finish (§5.6).
  6. The server sets the huzz_chat_session cookie and the app starts (§4.2).

Joining with an invite

  1. Someone already on the server taps Create invite link (or sends an email invite). The server makes a random 256-bit token, stores only its hash, and gives back a link (§1.3).
  2. They share the link or show it as a QR code.
  3. The new person opens it. By default it opens the front door's /join page, which shows the server's name and checks that the server's key fingerprint matches k= in the link.
  4. The page checks the token directly with the person's server (POST <server>/api/invite/check).
  5. The person picks a username and password on their own server's page (/welcome), which sends POST /api/welcome.
  6. The server creates the account, marks the invite used and makes them friends with the inviter.
  7. The app starts and creates this device's keys (§5.2).
📘Good To Know: Invite rules

An invite link works once, for 72 hours. The admin can cancel it at any time. After it is used, cancelled or re-sent, the server keeps a hash "tombstone" for 14 days so the page can say used or cancelled instead of a confusing error (docs/DIRECTORY.md, web/accounts.py:1278).

All the details

Passwords. scrypt with N=2^14, r=8, p=1, 32-byte output (accounts.hash_password, line 333). Minimum length BC_MIN_PASSWORD_LEN, default 12 (allowed 8–200) (web/bcconfig.py).

Session cookie. huzz_chat_session=<token>; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=SESSION_SECONDS (web/server.py line 9568). The token is base64url(JSON claims {u, v, exp, sid}) . HMAC-SHA256 keyed with STATE_DIR/session.key. The authoritative row is in sessions.json; a cookie whose row is gone is rejected. Lifetime BC_SESSION_DAYS, default 30 (1–400). Sessions slide: renewed when the time left is under min(13 days, 1/3 of the lifetime).

Verified-browser cookie. huzz_chat_verified (line 9573), 400 days (VERIFY_SECONDS). Lets a browser that already passed the email code skip it next time.

Sign-in flow:

Sign-up.

TOTP limits. The login-totp ticket lasts 300 s; wrong codes are limited to 5 per 15 minutes (FACTOR_FAILS_MAX = 5, FACTOR_WINDOW = 15*60; web/server.py:5619, web/accounts.py:1049-1050).

  • Invite: an admin or friend creates an invite (72 h; token stored hashed). The usual path is Create invite link (shown as a QR code or shared; no email). An email invite is also possible. The default link is https://twigum.app/join?s=<host>&n=<name>&k=<fingerprint>#t=<token>, which sends the person through the front door to the server; a direct /welcome#t=<token> link is used only for the home server itself, with BC_INVITE_DIRECT=1, or on http test installs (web/directory.py:56,328-339). The invitee posts POST /api/welcome {token, username, email, password} (web/server.py:6294-6312; accounts.accept_invite, line 1376; welcome.js:80-84,154-157). The new account is auto-friended with the inviter.
  • Public sign-up (public mode only): POST /api/signup with Cloudflare Turnstile when BC_SIGNUP_REQUIRE_CAPTCHA is on (publicmode.py).

Re-authentication (_device_reauth, line 6787). Sensitive actions (adding/changing a device key, removing devices, revoking other sessions, verifying devices) need a sign-in within the last 15 minutes (DEVICE_FRESH_SECONDS) or the password typed again; replacing or confirming a key backup always needs the typed password (require_password=True). Password tries are rate-limited (publicmode.login_try). A session at the device cap (no bound device) that removes a device key always needs the password, plus a TOTP code when two-factor is on (web/server.py:7195-7203). BC_LOGIN_CODE_EXEMPT is read from the process environment only, not from config.env (web/server.py:88).

3.7 Devices

🌱In plain words

Each phone, computer or browser you use Twigum on is a separate device with its own keys, like each family member having their own house key. The server keeps a list of each person's devices and their public keys (the part that is safe to share), so senders know who to lock messages for. You can have up to 8.

A device is one browser/app install with its own keys (§5.2). POST /api/devices registers {device_id, public_key (ECDH P-256), signing_public_key (ECDSA P-256), signatures}.

  • Maximum DEVICE_MAX = 8 per account. When full, only a key unused for more than 30 days (DEVICE_STALE_SECONDS) is evicted automatically; otherwise 409 too_many_devices.
  • A new or changed key needs fresh sign-in or the password (_device_reauth).
  • The signing key must be bound to the chat key (bind_sig, twigum-signing-bind-v1) or cross-signed by another of the account's devices (/api/devices/cross-sign, twigum-device-cross-v1). Verification is in web/device_sig.py.
  • The session is bound to its device (accounts.bind_session_device, line 510). If a session already bound to another device tries to attach a signing key, the session is ended (403 "Sign in again.").
  • Other people see a device as verified once its owner verified it (/api/devices/verify) or it was added through a verified path.

3.8 Sending photos, videos and files (uploads)

🌱In plain words

A big file is locked on your device with its own key and cut into pieces of 8 MiB (about the size of two phone photos). The pieces are sent one by one, so a slow connection can show progress and a large video does not have to arrive in one go. The key that unlocks the file travels inside the (locked) message, so only the people in the chat can open it. The server only ever stores locked pieces.

  1. The sender's app makes a random file key, cuts the file into 8 MiB pieces and locks each one (AES-GCM).
  2. It asks to start an upload (POST /api/blobs/start with the size). The server checks the size limit, the storage budget and free disk space.
  3. It sends each locked piece (POST /api/blobs/part), showing progress.
  4. It says it has finished (POST /api/blobs/finish).
  5. It sends the message, which carries the file's id and, inside the locked text, the file key.
  6. The recipient's app downloads the locked pieces (GET /api/blobs/<id>/<n>) and unlocks them with the key from the message.

Code: uploadBlob (web/static/app.js line 12301), postPart (12268), downloadPlain (12317); server blob_start (9320), blob_part (9365), blob_finish (9427), blob_get (9472). /api/blobs/part is the one POST where multipart/form-data passes the CSRF guard; it also needs a 128-bit upload id owned by the account (web/server.py:9388-9399).

The server never sees or checks the file type. blob_start reads only size and kind ("video" or empty), and kind is used only for eviction (web/server.py:9320-9363). The type label recipients see comes from the sender's app, inside the encrypted message.

Video playback (web/static/video-local.js:1-24, video-open.js:8-46, app.js:12626-12672):

  • The sender keeps the original in a per-session map (rememberLocalVideo, max 16) and plays it locally.
  • Videos over 80 MiB (INLINE_VIDEO_MAX), or of unknown size with no local copy, don't play inline: "This video is too large to play here. Use Save to keep it."
  • An evicted video returns 410 and shows "This video expired to free space." (§3.3 File retention).

Saving on iOS: the page's save goes through the injected bridge.js → bcSaveFile → DownloadHandler.swift / NativeFileSaver → the share sheet (Save Image / Save to Files). No Photos permission is needed, there is a 100 MiB cap, and a "Saved" toast is shown (DownloadHandler.swift:60-72; app.js:20238, 20435-20441).

Large media: originals over ORIGINAL_MAX (1 GiB) must be sent as HD/SD versions (client). Video playback uses web/static/video*.js; images can be edited before sending (mediaedit.js). DNG previews are decoded in a worker (web/tests/dng_preview_worker.test.mjs).

3.9 Notifications (push)

🌱In plain words

When a message arrives, the person's phone may be asleep. Push is a way to wake it. The server sends a tiny note through the phone maker's delivery service ("Apple, please tap this iPhone on the shoulder"). For browsers, the note says only "wake up"; the browser then fetches the message itself and unlocks it. Android does not use a delivery service at all: the app keeps checking quietly by itself.

Web Push (web/webpush.py): VAPID key pair in vapid.json, subscriptions in push.json (max 8 per account, MAX_PER_USER), log push.log. The payload is a fixed wake-up {"v":1}, encrypted per RFC 8291, sent with curl (HTTP/2), TTL 86400, Urgency high. 404/410 responses drop the subscription. Endpoints are allow-listed (FCM web-push endpoint, Mozilla, *.push.apple.com, Windows). The service worker (web/sw.js, push handler line 572) wakes, fetches /api/sync with the session cookie, and decrypts with the device key in IndexedDB to show the text (an unsigned, badly signed or undecryptable row shows only "New message"). Safari cancels subscriptions whose pushes show nothing, so on Safari a push that found nothing new shows a silent "You're up to date." placeholder and closes it at once (quietPlaceholder).

APNs (web/apnspush.py) for the iOS app:

Setting Default Meaning
APNS_KEY_PATH — Path to the .p8 auth key (secret; not in repo)
APNS_KEY_ID — Key ID (not in repo)
APNS_TEAM_ID 2M4LH666X3 Apple Team ID
APNS_TOPIC app.branchchat.ios Bundle ID
APNS_PRODUCTION 1 Production vs sandbox gateway

The alert is visible text: "New message from ", or "New message" if the name is empty, longer than 64 characters or has control characters (web/server.py:8167, 1020-1029; apnspush.py:224-228). Apple also always sees the top-level chat key in clear (dm:<sender username>, g:<group id> or lobby). Only for signed Megolm rows with a dm:/g: chat key does the payload also carry m: {sid, b, sg, n, sd, i, c} (session id, ciphertext, signature, counter, sender device, index, chat; no plaintext) with mutable-content, so the Notification Service extension can decrypt a preview on the phone (§6.1.2; apnspush.py:263-276). Megolm needs BC_VODOZEMAC=1, which is off unless you turn it on, so by default iOS shows the generic text. Tokens are in apns.json, log in apns.log.

Not sent for muted chats or during the recipient's Do Not Disturb (post_message). Android has no server push (§6.2). Admin webhooks (dmwebhook.notify) can also wake bots.

3.10 Bug reports

POST /api/bug-report (web/bugreports.py:64-123; client app.js:22253-22301) is the user-started Report a bug form. It sends a description, steps, where it happened, up to 4 screenshots of at most 5 MiB each, and an environment block (layout, viewport, platform, standalone, theme, client_version). The server adds the server name, URL and version, the username and the User-Agent. Body up to 24 MiB, 20 reports per account per day. Stored as STATE_DIR/bug-reports/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl with screenshots in bug-reports/shots/. No logs or heartbeats are sent.

Device status reports: there is no such feature (checked in the code). What exists: bug reports (above), /api/account/sessions (sign-ins with names and last use), device lists in /api/sync, and the Administrator page overview.

3.11 Settings (configuration)

🌱In plain words

Configuration means the settings that change how the server behaves, such as its name, its web address or the largest file allowed. Each setting has a name in capital letters (like BC_PUBLIC_URL) and a value. The server looks for each one in three places, in this order, and uses the first it finds: 1) the environment it was started with, 2) the settings file config.env, 3) the built-in default.

Precedence (web/bcconfig.py): environment variable → config file → default. The config file is $BC_CONFIG, else /etc/branch-chat/config.env, else $BC_STATE_DIR/config.env. Secrets can come from <NAME>_FILE (get_secret). The Administrator page edits a schema of 91 settings and writes config.env on Apply (web/adminpage.py SCHEMA, lines 79-239), with a backup in config-backups/.

Environment-only settings. These are read from the process environment only, so setting them in config.env or on the Administrator page does nothing: BC_LOGIN_CODE_EXEMPT (web/server.py:88), BC_SIGNUP_REQUIRE_CAPTCHA (publicmode.py:133), BC_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED (memberwebhook.py:111; a stored flag also wins), BC_MEMBER_WEBHOOKS (:114), BC_WEBHOOKS_PATH, BC_SECRETS_DIR, BC_MEMBER_WEBHOOKS_PATH, and BC_VERSION (bcconfig.py:120).

Key settings (Appendix B lists every variable found):

Variable Default Effect
BC_HOST, BC_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8766 Bind address
BC_STATE_DIR /var/lib/huzz-chat State directory
BC_PUBLIC_URL http://localhost:8766 Public URL; https enables HSTS and redirects
BC_HOSTS — Extra allowed Host names
BC_OWNER admin Owner account
BC_MAIL_* mode sendmail / smtp / log; from Twigum <noreply@localhost> Outgoing mail
BC_SESSION_DAYS 30 (1–400) Session lifetime
BC_MIN_PASSWORD_LEN 12 (8–200) Password policy
BC_LOGIN_CODE_EXEMPT — Skip the email code for listed accounts (environment only)
BC_FILE_MAX_MB 2048 Max file size
BC_STORE_BUDGET_GB 10 File storage budget
BC_KEY_BACKUP_MODE recovery_key recovery_key / recovery_key_or_passphrase / legacy (§5.6)

BC_VODOZEMAC 0 Olm/Megolm. Experimental. Code says only "default off"; server/config.env.example:73 says to use it on a test server only
BC_VODOZEMAC_ACCEPT_LEGACY 1 Accept non-Megolm sends while vodozemac is on

🛠️Step by step: Change a setting

Where: on the server, in a terminal (bash). What it does: changes one setting and restarts Twigum so it takes effect.

Easiest way: sign in as the owner, open https://chat.example.com/admin, change the setting and press Apply. The page saves config.env, keeps the old copy in config-backups/, restarts the server, and puts the old file back if the server fails to start.

By hand (native install):

  1. Open the file in a text editor: sudo nano /etc/branch-chat/config.env
  2. Find the line (for example BC_FILE_MAX_MB=2048) or add a new line at the end, in the form NAME=value with no spaces around =.
  3. Save: press Ctrl+O, Enter, then Ctrl+X to leave.
  4. Restart: sudo systemctl restart branch-chat
  5. Check: sudo /opt/branch-chat/install.sh status should say the service is active, and curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version should answer.
  6. If it fails: sudo /opt/branch-chat/install.sh logs shows the last error. Undo your change and restart again.

By hand (Docker): edit config.env next to docker-compose.yml, then run sudo docker compose up -d in that folder (Docker recreates the container with the new settings).

⚠️Warning: Some settings are ignored in config.env

The environment-only settings listed above (for example BC_LOGIN_CODE_EXEMPT and BC_SIGNUP_REQUIRE_CAPTCHA) are read only from the process environment. Putting them in config.env or on the Administrator page does nothing.

3.12 Security headers and request guards

🌱In plain words

Headers are short notes the server attaches to every answer, telling the browser how to behave safely: "only run code that came from me", "always use the locked (https) connection", "don't let other sites put me in a frame". They protect people even if something else goes wrong.

Headers come from web/server.py; there is no nginx header config in the repo.

  • CSP on HTML (web/server.py CSP): default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' blob: data:; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://www.youtube.com https://ko-fi.com; media-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self' blob: data:; worker-src 'self'; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. Front-door and sign-up pages add https://challenges.cloudflare.com to script-src, frame-src and connect-src for Turnstile (frontdoor.py:427-434, publicmode.py:323-325).
  • HSTS max-age=31536000 on every response when the public URL is https and BC_HSTS is not 0; includeSubDomains only with BC_HSTS_SUBDOMAINS=1 (default 0) (web/server.py:93-96, 4224-4229).
  • X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on all responses.
  • Host check (host_ok, line 4214) against HOSTS; unknown hosts get 404.
  • CSRF guard (post_guard_ok, line 4492) on POST/PUT/DELETE to /api/* only (web/server.py:4492-4526): checks Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site, refuses "simple" content types (form posts) except multipart on /api/blobs/part, and allows cross-origin POST to /api/invite/check from the directory home origins.
  • No compression of HTML or JSON (BREACH); only static CSS/JS/SVG/WASM is gzip/brotli-compressed.
  • Cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax.

3.13 Logs

🌱In plain words

A log is the server's diary: a list of what happened and when, mostly errors. Twigum keeps its diary short on purpose: it does not write down who visited which page, so the log cannot be used to track people.

  • Handler.log_message is silenced: request lines are not logged (no IP addresses or paths). Exception: the home-network admin listener prints directory admin audit: lines with the caller's address and path (directory.py:1336,1349).
  • Errors: Python tracebacks go to standard output, which systemd's journal or Docker collects. People only ever see one-sentence errors.
  • Admin actions: lines starting with admin audit: (_audit).
  • Push: push.log and apns.log in STATE_DIR (endpoints and tokens are not written).
🛠️Step by step: Read the server's log

Where: on the server (bash). What it does: shows the newest lines of Twigum's log. It changes nothing.

  • Native or Docker install made by the installer: sudo /opt/branch-chat/install.sh logs
  • Native, by hand: sudo journalctl -u branch-chat -n 200 --no-pager (add -f to follow live; Ctrl+C to stop).
  • Docker, by hand: in the folder with docker-compose.yml, run sudo docker compose logs --tail 200 branch-chat.

You should see lines with dates. A healthy server is mostly quiet. Lines starting with Traceback are errors; copy the last few lines when you ask for help, and check that they contain no passwords first.

3.14 How a server talks to the public front door (directory and invites)

🌱In plain words

Think of the front door at twigum.app as a town notice board. A family's server can pin a card on it that says "The Smith Family chat is here, and here is our seal". Every five minutes the server touches the card to say "still here". If the touches stop, the card is taken down after 15 minutes. The board checks the seal so nobody can pin up a fake card for someone else's server. The board never holds anyone's messages or passwords; it only points the way.

The public front door at twigum.app is run by the Twigum project. Your server is an organisation server (it reports to the front door if you turn that on); twigum.app is the home.

There are three connections between an organisation server and the front door. Only the first is optional.

What Direction When What is sent
Directory listing ("lease ping") your server → front door every BC_DIRECTORY_PING_SECONDS (300 s, ±30 s), only if BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=1 your server's address, the time, online yes/no, its public key and a signature. Nothing else.
Key check ("first contact") front door → your server the first time it sees your key, then every 6 hours the front door reads https://<your server>/.well-known/branchchat and checks that the key there matches the ping
Invite landing the invitee's browser → both when someone opens an invite link the browser shows the front door's /join page and asks your server directly whether the token is valid. The token itself never goes to the front door.
  1. Your server signs a ping. It contains {"v":2, "login_url":"https://chat.example.com/", "ts":<now>, "online":true, "key":"<public key>", "sig":"<signature>"}. The signature covers bc-lease-v2, the address, the time and online/offline, made with the private key in STATE_DIR/server-identity.json (an Ed25519 key, made on first use, file mode 600, never sent anywhere).
  2. It sends the ping to POST <BC_HOME_URL>/api/directory/lease. BC_HOME_URL is https://twigum.app by default (web/directory.py:57).
  3. The front door checks the ping and refuses it if: it has unknown fields; the time is more than 120 s off (stale); the time is not newer than the last ping for that key (replay); the signature is wrong; the key is revoked; the host is banned; or a different key is already listed live for that address (409).
  4. First contact (trust on first use): the first time, the front door fetches https://chat.example.com/.well-known/branchchat and requires identity_key there to equal the key in the ping. It re-checks every 6 hours. A server on a private or unreachable address stays pending until the front door's operator vouches for it after comparing the fingerprint by other means.
  5. Listed. The listing shows while the last ping is younger than BC_DIRECTORY_TTL (900 s = three missed pings). Name and icon are read live from your server (cached 10 minutes). Listings with no ping for 30 days are forgotten.
  6. People can pick it. The server now appears in the front door's directory (/directory, /api/directory), and the iPhone/iPad app is allowed to save it (§1.4).

The front door stores only each server's key, address, last ping time, last timestamp, verified flags and hide/ban flags (docs/DIRECTORY.md). Rate limits: 120 pings per hour per address, 3 per 50 s per host and key, 120 lookups per 10 minutes per address (memory only).

📘Good To Know: The fingerprint in your invite links

The key fingerprint is a short code made from your server's public key: b64url(sha256("bc-identity-v1:" + key)), first 32 characters. Invite links carry its first 12 characters as k=. The /join page refuses a link whose k does not match the server's real key, so a tampered link cannot send people to an impostor server.

⚠️Warning: Losing server-identity.json loses your listing

If server-identity.json is lost (for example a new install without restoring a backup), your server makes a new key. While the old listing is still live, the front door refuses the new key for the same address (409). Wait until the old listing expires (15 minutes after the last good ping), or restore the file from a backup (§7.11). Old invite links also stop working because their k= no longer matches.

The invite link, step by step

invite_link() (web/directory.py:328-339) always builds links through the front door's landing page, whether or not your server is listed (since 26.10.10; the comment explains this lets the Twigum Android app, which only trusts the front door's links, catch every server's invites):

https://twigum.app/join?s=chat.example.com&n=The%20Smith%20Family&k=<12 chars>#t=<token>

A direct link https://chat.example.com/welcome#t=<token> is used instead only when:

  • BC_INVITE_DIRECT=1, or
  • the server's own address is plain http:// and reporting is off (test installs), or
  • the server is the home (BC_HOME_URL).

On the landing page the browser:

  1. shows your server's real address, plus the name and icon from the verified listing, else from your server's own /.well-known/branchchat, else from the link (marked "not verified");
  2. refuses if k does not match the key fingerprint;
  3. checks the token with POST https://chat.example.com/api/invite/check (your server allows this cross-site call only from the home origins: BC_HOME_URL, https://twigum.app and https://branchchat.app, web/directory.py:60-66);
  4. sends the person to https://chat.example.com/welcome#t=<token>&u=<username> to create the account, or https://chat.example.com/#u=<username> to sign in.

The password is only ever typed on your own server.

📘Good To Know: docs/DIRECTORY.md

docs/DIRECTORY.md matches this section: the default home is https://twigum.app, invite links go through the home unless one of the three exceptions above applies, and https://branchchat.app stays a valid home (it does not redirect to twigum.app yet).

🛠️Step by step: Check your server's directory status

Where: on your server (bash). What it does: prints whether reporting is on, the home URL, your name and icon, your public key and fingerprint, and the result of the last ping. It changes nothing.

Native install:

sudo -u branchchat BC_CONFIG=/etc/branch-chat/config.env BC_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/branch-chat \
  python3 /opt/branch-chat/app/manage.py directory-status

Docker install (made by the installer):

sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml -p branch-chat exec branch-chat python manage.py directory-status

You should see lines like reporting: on, home url: https://twigum.app, identity key: … (fingerprint …) and last ping: 14:05:12 ….

If it fails: reporting: off means BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT is not 1 (§3.11). A last ping message with an error usually means the time on the server is wrong (more than 120 s off: turn on time sync with sudo timedatectl set-ntp true) or the front door cannot reach /.well-known/branchchat on your address.

Related commands (same prefix): directory-ping (send one ping now; --offline tells the home you are going offline), directory-pause --minutes N (stop pinging for N minutes, so the listing drops off), directory-resume.

4. The app (web client), inside

🌱In plain words

The app is a web page that behaves like an app. When you open Twigum, your browser (or the phone app's built-in browser) downloads the app's code from your server, then runs it on your device. All the clever parts, such as making keys, locking and unlocking messages and drawing the chats, happen on your device, not on the server.

4.1 The files that make up the app

The app is plain JavaScript (the language web pages are programmed in), split into ES modules (files that load each other), with no build step and no framework: the files in the repo are exactly what the browser runs. The server fills in a few placeholders as it sends them ({{BC_VERSION}}, {{BC_VERSION_SPOKEN}}, {{BC_SHELL}}, {{BC_ASSET}}, {{BC_KOFI_URL}}, {{BC_PW_MIN}}; web/server.py lines ~122–161).

File Role
web/index.html Signed-in app shell (chat list, chat view, menus)
web/login.html, web/static/login.js Sign-in, code entry, key-backup restore
web/welcome.html, web/static/welcome.js Invite sign-up
web/static/app.js Main app: boot, sync, rendering, composer, media, settings (25,214 lines)
web/static/crypto.js All cryptography (§5)
web/static/vodozemac*.js, web/static/vendor/vodozemac/ Olm/Megolm, lazy-loaded WASM (flag-gated)
web/static/row-context.js Per-row context menus
web/static/account-guard.js Detects a different account signing in within the same tab, then reloads
web/static/share-picker.js Share-in flow (Android/iOS/web share target). share-attach.js is not in web/static: it is a native script the apps inject (android/app/src/main/assets/share-attach.js, ios/Twigum/Resources/share-attach.js)
web/static/public.js Public-mode helpers (Lobby text masking until the filter list is loaded)
web/static/menu-precache.js Pre-caches menu images
web/static/video*.js, mediaedit.js, stickers.js Media playback, editing, stickers
web/static/health-retry.js, offline-retry.js Offline page retry logic
web/static/app.css (+ dir.css, gate.css, host.css, boot-splash.css) Styles
web/sw.js Service worker (§4.7)

4.2 What happens when the app opens (startup)

  1. Settings first. boot() (app.js line 14504) applies the light/dark mode, colours, text size and layout, so the screen looks right straight away.
  2. Find this device's keys in IndexedDB (huzz-chat / kv, key device). If there are none, this is a new device: createIdentity makes a new chat key and device id.
  3. Make sure there is a signing key (ensureSigningKey, ECDSA P-256; its private half can never be copied out of the browser).
  4. Register the device with the server in the background (bootDeviceRegister: POST /api/devices; one automatic try, then a Retry button, at most 3 per page load, waiting 2 s and doubling up to 30 s).
  5. At the same time, show the chats (continueBoot, line 14572): check that the same account is still signed in (accountGuard.boot), load the locked copy of recent messages from the browser (histLoad, IndexedDB bc-history), do the first /api/sync and draw the chat list.
  6. Start the sync loop (§3.5), open the chat in the link if there is one (?open=), turn on notifications, load the profile and paint the background.

boot() (web/static/app.js line 14504) and continueBoot() (line 14572):

Notes:

  • The chat list does not wait for device registration (bootDeviceRegister runs in parallel).
  • If POST /api/devices answers 403 {error: "Sign in again.", need_reauth: true} (the session is bound to another device), the client clears the session and shows sign-in, keeping keys and history (isSessionBindingReauth).
  • The local history cache (bc-history, app.js ~line 120) stores ciphertext only, per account, so a reload asks the server only for changes. It is cleared on logout and when another account signs in.

4.3 What the app keeps on the device

🌱In plain words

The app keeps a few things in the browser's own storage: the device's keys (the most important thing), a locked copy of recent messages so chats open fast, and your preferences. Clearing the browser's "site data" for your Twigum address removes all of this, including the keys. If you have no key backup, old messages cannot be opened afterwards.

Store Contents
IndexedDB huzz-chat, object store kv device (ECDH key pair, device id, ECDSA signing key — the signing private key is a non-extractable CryptoKey), send-counter:<account>:<device>, replay ledger, notify-mute, notify-seq, notify-keys-off, the per-account device-pins record (other people's signing-key pins, each with its previous keys; ensurePinMap/savePins, app.js:1803-1823), vodozemac records (vodo-account|olm|inbound|outbound-<device>, sealed with a non-extractable per-device key)
IndexedDB bc-history (v2), stores rows (index by_seq) and meta Ciphertext rows and sync cursors
localStorage UI preferences (bc-virt, bc-last-chat, palette, mute), drafts
sessionStorage bc-open (pending chat to open)
Cache Storage bc-shell-<SHELL_V>, bc-static-<SHELL_V>, bc-ambient (§4.7)

4.4 Chat list and messages

  • Chats: Lobby (public room), direct messages, groups. Client chat keys are lobby, dm:<peer> and g:<id>; dm:<a>:<b> and group:<id> are server-side scopes only (app.js:507-513; web/server.py:983). Chat-list order, pins and archive sync across devices (/api/chats/list, chatlist in sync). Unread counts come from read marks (/api/read, readmarks.json).
  • Rows are decrypted on the client, checked (signature, counter, replay), then rendered. renderLog() (line 10663) draws the message log.
  • Per-chat drafts, replies, reactions (setupReact), edits, deletes, pinned messages and receipts are handled in app.js.

4.5 Long chats (virtual scrolling)

🌱In plain words

A chat can have tens of thousands of messages. Drawing all of them at once would make the phone slow. So the app only draws the messages near what you are looking at, plus a few extra above and below, and leaves empty space of the right height for the rest. As you scroll, it swaps messages in and out. This is called virtual scrolling.

Long chats are virtualised: only the rows near the viewport are in the DOM, with spacer elements above and below.

Constant Value Meaning
LOG_FIRST 120 Size of the log window (newest rows decrypted and considered) when a chat opens; only rows near the viewport are mounted
LOG_STEP 150 How much the window grows when scrolling up (app.js:10188-10198)
LOG_OVERSCAN 18 Extra rows above/below the viewport
LOG_VIRT_MIN 400 Chats shorter than this are not virtualised

Row heights are cached for spacer sizes. Android defaults to full mount (no virtualisation). Debug switches: window.__bcNoVirt or localStorage["bc-virt"]. Tests: web/tests/log_virt_spacers.test.mjs, virt_jump_pin.test.mjs, kid_filter_virt_rows.test.mjs.

4.6 Colours and backgrounds

  • Light/dark mode (html[data-scheme]), text size, chat layout, and colour palettes (applyPalette): huzz (default), glacier, nebula, lagoon, bubble, aubergine, vinyl, graphite, forest, ocean, sunset, lavender, ember, midnight, rose, mint.
  • Default dark theme variables (web/static/app.css :root): --bg #10141a, --card #1a212b, --line #354153, --text #f2f6fb, --mine #3c92ea (own bubbles), --other #3a4250, --accent #9ec0ff, --danger #ff5d5d.
  • Logo font "BC Outfit" (web/static/outfit.woff, variable weight 100–900) for the .bc-logo wordmark, with the green #7cc98c accent.
  • Chat backgrounds/wallpapers: paintBackground() (line 14091); per-server branding via /instance.css and /instance/background. Ambient audio files are cached in bc-ambient.

4.7 Working offline and updating itself (service worker)

🌱In plain words

The service worker (sw.js) is a small helper the browser keeps running for the app. It keeps a copy of the app's files, so the app opens even with no internet, and it shows notifications. When a new version is released, every file gets a new "stamp", the helper fetches the new copy, throws away the old one and tells open pages to reload.

web/sw.js (registered as a module at scope / with updateViaCache: "none", app.js line 4445):

Request Strategy
Non-GET, other origins Not handled (browser default)
Paths matching NEVER (/api, /auth, /login, /logout, /push, /upload(s), /blob, /ws, /sw.js, /manifest.webmanifest, /share, /.well-known) Not handled — always network
Navigations Network-first; on failure or edge gateway errors (502/503/504/520–524) serve /offline.html, which retries /api/version with backoff
/instance.css Network-first, cached copy offline
/static/ambient/* bc-ambient cache (not versioned)
/static/* Cache-first in bc-static-<SHELL_V>

SHELL_V is {{BC_SHELL}} = VERSION + "-" + fingerprint of the served pages and app code. Every release (or page change) gives new cache names. On activate, older bc-shell-* / bc-static-* caches are deleted and open pages get postMessage({type: "bc-sw-updated"}) so they reload with the new code. Static URLs carry ?v={{BC_ASSET}} (same stamp); a match gets Cache-Control: immutable, max-age=1 year.

The What's New pop-up after an update reads web/static/whatsnew/<VERSION>.json (§7.1.1). The file is required for every release by team rule. tools/release-check.py only warns when it is missing. It fails when the file is broken (version mismatch, no title/sections, or an item without title/text) or when whatsnew/index.json is stale; it then regenerates the index, which you commit (tools/release-check.py:200-217).

4.8 Offline behaviour

  • The app shell and static files work offline; offline.html is shown when navigation fails.
  • Cached history (bc-history) lets a reload show earlier chats quickly; sending needs the network (failed sends can be retried).
  • Native wrappers show their own "could not be reached / Try again" screens (Android MainActivity, iOS WebViewController).

4.9 What the app can ask the phone or computer to do (native bridges)

🌱In plain words

A bridge is a small, guarded doorway between the web app and the native app around it. Through it, the web page can ask for things a web page normally can't do, such as "save this file to the phone" or "show me the list of servers". The native app only opens the doorway for pages from servers it trusts.

The page feature-detects each bridge.

Platform Bridge Methods / messages

Android (internal) Java object window.BranchChatApp (also window.TwigumApp, MainActivity.java:333-334); every call needs a random per-launch token. Used inside bridge.js and share-attach.js, not by the page pendingShare/doneShare, setNotifyKey, openNotifySetup, saveBegin/saveChunk/saveEnd/saveEndOpen/saveAbort/saveFailed/saveBase64/saveError/saveLastError, setFullscreen, … (NativeBridge.java)

It wraps the window.webkit.messageHandlers registered at WebViewController.swift:91-100 (bcShare, bcPushPermission, bcMegolm, bcClearKeys, bcReadAccount, bcSaveFile, bcReadClear, reply handler bcServers, and the share hand-off bcShareFiles, ShareHandoff.swift:25) platform: "ios", pushToken, requestPushPermission, putMegolmSession, clearNotifyKeys, setSignedInAccount, clearChatNotify, share, listServers, openServer, addServer, removeServer
