5. Encryption and security

🌱In plain words

Encryption turns a message into scrambled text that looks like nonsense. Only someone with the right key can turn it back. Twigum uses three ideas, and each has an everyday picture:

  • A padlock and its key (symmetric encryption). Each message is locked with a brand-new random key. The same key locks and unlocks it.
  • A letterbox with a slot (public-key encryption). Every device has a key pair: a public key that works like a letterbox slot anyone can drop things into, and a private key that is the only key to open the letterbox. The sender puts a copy of the message's padlock key through each recipient device's slot. That copy is called a wrap.
  • A wax seal (signatures). Each device also has a signing key. It stamps every message with a seal that only that device can make, and anyone can check. If someone changes the message, or pretends to be the sender, the seal does not match.

The server stores the locked messages and the wraps, but never the private keys, so it cannot open them. The precise rules, and the exceptions, follow.

All cryptography runs on the device: the browser's built-in WebCrypto in web/static/crypto.js, plus vodozemac (WASM) when that switch is on. The server stores ciphertext, public keys and signatures, and checks signatures (web/device_sig.py mirrors the byte formats in crypto.js).

5.1 The building blocks (primitives)

A primitive is one basic cryptographic tool. Plain-words names are in brackets; the glossary (§10) explains each one.

  • ECDH P-256 (the letterbox: a way for two key pairs to agree on a shared secret)
  • ECDSA P-256 (the wax seal: signatures)
  • AES-256-GCM (the padlock: fast locking that also detects tampering)
  • HKDF / PBKDF2 (key "stretchers" that turn one secret into a proper key; PBKDF2 is deliberately slow so passwords can't be guessed quickly)
  • SHA-256 (a fingerprint machine: any input gives a fixed-size code, and you can't go backwards)
Use Algorithm Where
Device chat key (identity) ECDH P-256 (private key extractable, so it can go into a key backup) createIdentity (crypto.js line 34)
Device signing key ECDSA P-256, non-extractable (not in key backups) ensureSigningKey (line 478)
Message content AES-256-GCM with a fresh random 32-byte key per message; AAD = messageAad(senderDevice, conversation, counter) ("twigum-msg-aad-v1") for signed messages sealSigned (app.js ~2487), encryptJson
Key wrap to a device Ephemeral ECDH P-256 → HKDF-SHA256 (salt huzz-chat-salt-v1, info huzz-chat-wrap-v1) → AES-256-GCM. Output {eph_pub, iv, ct} wrapFor / unwrap (lines 73, 91)
Group / Lobby epoch key Random 32-byte key per epoch, wrapped per member device with wrapFor; the message key is encrypted under it (epoch_iv, epoch_ct) epochKeyFor, groupKeyFor (app.js)
Files Random file key; 8 MiB chunks, each AES-GCM with a 12-byte IV prefix encryptChunk (line 137)
Key backup v2 AES-GCM, AAD branchchat-backup:v2:<kind>; key from recovery key (HKDF info branchchat-backup-v2-rk) or passphrase (PBKDF2-SHA256, ≥600,000 rounds) sealRecovery, openRecovery, sealBackup, openBackup
Key backup v1 (legacy) Sealed with the login password (PBKDF2-SHA256, 200,000 rounds) crypto.js line ~165
Fingerprints First 80 bits of SHA-256 of the SPKI public key; safety numbers (branchchat-safety-v1) keyFingerprint, safetyNumber
Device SAS Short code + emoji derived locally from both public keys and the request id deriveDeviceSas (line 437)
Olm / Megolm (flag) vodozemac (Curve25519 / Ed25519; Megolm ratchet) crates/vodozemac-js, web/static/vodozemac*.js

Signed byte formats (canonical newline-joined strings, crypto.js ↔ web/device_sig.py):

Label Signs
twigum-device-v1 A device record (user, device id, chat public key, signing public key, created)
twigum-device-cross-v1 One own device vouching for another (also user, created and the signer's device id) (crypto.js:504-525)
twigum-signing-bind-v1 Chat key binding the signing key
twigum-msg-v1 Message: sender device, conversation, sorted recipient device ids, counter, iv, ct, sorted wrap lines (messageBytes, line 605)
twigum-rewrap-v1 A later wrap of a signed message for a new device
twigum-vodo-id-v1 A device's Olm identity: user, device_id, curve25519, ed25519; signed by its signing key (crypto.js:775-783)
twigum-megolm-v1 A Megolm message: sender device, conversation, counter, session id and Megolm body. The message index is not signed; it is checked separately against the body (crypto.js:801-812; MegolmPreview.swift:202,211)

5.2 The keys each device has

Each install is a device with:

  1. Device id — 16 random bytes, hex.
  2. Chat key — ECDH P-256 key pair. Used to unwrap message keys and epoch keys.
  3. Signing key — ECDSA P-256, non-extractable. Signs messages and device records.
  4. Optional Olm account (vodozemac) — sealed in IndexedDB under a non-extractable per-device key.

They live in IndexedDB huzz-chat / kv under device (§4.3). Native apps get copies of specific keys only for notifications (§5.7).

5.3 Adding a new device and trusting it

🌱In plain words

When you sign in on a new phone, it makes its own new keys. Your friends' apps see a new letterbox appear on your account. To stop a bad server from slipping in a fake letterbox, the new device must be signed in recently (or type the password), its keys must be sealed together, and your other devices can vouch for it. Your friends' apps remember each device's seal the first time they see it (key pinning). If a seal ever changes, they block that device's messages until a person confirms the change.

  1. The new device makes its keys (createIdentity, ensureSigningKey).
  2. It registers them (POST /api/devices) with the signatures that tie the chat key and signing key together.
  3. The server checks: signed in within 15 minutes or password typed (_device_reauth); at most 8 devices (one unused for 30 days can be replaced, else 409); the signatures are valid (device_sig.py). It then ties the session to this device.
  4. To read old messages, the new device needs the old chat keys: from the key backup (§5.6), or (with BC_DEVICE_APPROVAL=1) from an existing device that approves it after both screens show the same short code and emoji.
  5. An existing own device can cross-sign the new one (POST /api/devices/cross-sign). That also allows your other devices to re-wrap old direct messages for it (§3.4.6).
  6. Friends' apps receive the device list in /api/sync and pin the new signing key.

Trust rules on the receiving side (crypto.js judgeMessage, trustedPin, acceptClassicRow; app.js rejectedNotice):

  • Each sender device's signing key is pinned on first sight (key pin, stored only on your device in IndexedDB device-pins). Signed rows must verify under the pin, with matching counter and AAD.
  • Unsigned rows from a device that never had a signing key (or sent before it had one) stay readable but are labelled unverified. An unsigned row is rejected as unsigned only if the pin already had a signing key at that time (crypto.js:649-704, 1067-1092).
  • Rejection reasons shown in chat: changed-key ("…'s device key changed. Messages from it are blocked until you re-confirm."), replay, unsigned, downgrade, bad signature (texts in §9).
  • Signing outage label. Only unsigned rows that would otherwise be rejected can get "Sent during the signing outage — sender not verified", and only if all of these hold (crypto.js:1011-1014, 1036-1064, 1078-1086):
    • the row's ts (and any edit ts) is inside the window SIGNING_OUTAGE_START 1794271200 to SIGNING_OUTAGE_END 1794428710 (9 Nov 2026 4:40 PM PST to 11 Nov 2026 12:25 PM PST; values frozen);
    • the pin is trusted, not revoked, and had a signing key with signing_since ≤ ts;
    • signing_adopted_at is absent or ≤ ts;
    • the device's first_seen is before the window start;
    • the device and user match the pin;
    • the message id and body were not seen before.

5.4 Sending and receiving a message

  1. The sender's app makes a fresh 32-byte message key and the next send counter (a number that only goes up, so old messages can't be replayed).
  2. It locks the message with AES-GCM, binding in the sender device, the chat and the counter.
  3. It wraps the message key for every device of the recipient(s) and for the sender's own other devices.
  4. It seals everything with the device's signing key (twigum-msg-v1).
  5. It sends it (POST /api/messages). The server runs the checks in §3.4.6 and stores it.
  6. The recipient's app is woken (§3.5) and fetches the new row.
  7. It checks the seal against the pinned key and the counter against its replay list.
  8. It unwraps its own copy of the message key and unlocks the message. If any check fails, it shows a notice instead (§9).

Send counter (nextSendCounter, app.js line 2264): the next counter is the maximum of the stored counter + 1, any legacy counter + 1, the highest own counter seen + 1, the page floor + 1, and Date.now(). It is stored in IndexedDB under send-counter:<account>:<device>. The server refuses a reused (sender_device, ctr) with 422 ctr_reused and the highest counter it has; withCounterRetry (line 2293) bumps and resends once. The receiver's replay ledger (createReplayLedger, crypto.js line 915) refuses a counter it has already accepted.

DMs wrap the message key to every device of both people. Groups and the Lobby use an epoch key: the message key is encrypted with the current epoch key; the epoch key is wrapped once per member device. Membership changes start a new epoch:

  • Lobby join → new epoch, so the joiner cannot read older Lobby messages (lobby_join). Leave → new epoch.
  • Group add → next epoch wrapped for the new member set; remove → next epoch wrapped only for those who stay; link join → new empty epoch that the joiner or any member fills (group_add, group_remove, glink_redeem). The first member to post wraps for an empty epoch wins (lobby_epoch, group_epoch).

5.5 The newer lock: Megolm / vodozemac (off by default)

🌱In plain words

Megolm is a second way of locking group chats, used by other well-known secure chat apps. Instead of a new padlock key for every message, it uses a key that changes a little with every message, like a combination lock that automatically moves to a new number each time. vodozemac is the library that does this. In Twigum it is still experimental and switched off.

Item Status at this commit
Flag BC_VODOZEMAC, default 0. The code only says "default off" (web/server.py:238; vodozemac_proto.py:32). server/config.env.example:73 says to use it on a test server only (experimental).
Scope DMs and private groups. The Lobby stays on the epoch (ck) path.
When used A client sends alg: "megolm" only when every device it would reach advertises megolm.v1 (caps on /api/vodo/keys/upload). Otherwise the legacy envelope.
Legacy BC_VODOZEMAC_ACCEPT_LEGACY=1 (default) keeps accepting legacy sends. With 0, legacy sends get "This app version can't send here any more. Update Twigum and try again." Old rows always stay readable (dual-read).

5.6 Key backup: reading old messages on a new device

🌱In plain words

Your keys live only on your devices. If you lose all of them, the locked messages on the server can't be opened any more, by anyone. A key backup is a locked copy of your keys that the server keeps for you. It is locked with a recovery key: a long code (56 letters and numbers) that only you have, like the spare key you leave with a trusted neighbour, except the neighbour (the server) can't use it. Write the recovery key down and keep it safe.

  1. The person signs in with password and email code.
  2. Because the account has a backup, the server sends the locked backup and a one-time ticket.
  3. The person types their recovery key (or backup passphrase).
  4. The app turns it into the unlocking key (HKDF or PBKDF2), opens the backup and stores the recovered chat keys.
  5. It finishes signing in (POST /api/login/finish).
  6. It starts as usual, and old messages unlock.

A new device can only read old messages if it gets the old chat keys. The key backup holds the account's device chat keys, sealed on the device.

Mode (BC_KEY_BACKUP_MODE) How it is sealed Can the server open it?
recovery_key (default) v2, 256-bit recovery key shown to the person as 56 Crockford base32 characters with a check No
recovery_key_or_passphrase v2, recovery key or a separate backup passphrase (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000–5,000,000 rounds; server enforces the range) No
legacy Also allows v1 uploads (sealed with the login password); v2 recovery-key/passphrase uploads are still accepted v1: yes in principle (the server sees the password at sign-in)

In the two non-legacy modes, v1 uploads are refused ("Update the app…"). v1 backups can still be opened in any mode, for migration only (web/server.py:517-546; crypto.js:286-290).

Rules (save_key_backup, line 6167; confirm_key_backup_request):

  • Saving or replacing a backup always needs the typed account password.
  • A new backup is pending until a client opens it and confirms it by tag (first 32 hex of SHA-256 of its ciphertext) with the password. Until then the previous working copy is kept (backup_prev).
  • Password reset archives the backup (archive_key_backup) rather than deleting it.
⚠️Warning: No recovery key, no old messages

If someone loses every device and their recovery key, nobody (not the server admin, not the Twigum developers) can open their old messages. This is the price of the server not being able to read them. Remind people to save the recovery key when the app shows it.

5.7 What notifications show

Platform What the person sees How
Web (non-Safari) Message text sw.js decrypts with the device key from IndexedDB; falls back to "New message"
Safari / iOS web Text, or silent placeholder as above
iOS app "New message from " / "New message". Decrypted text only for signed Megolm DMs/groups when the session key is on the phone. Megolm needs BC_VODOZEMAC=1 (off by default), so by default iOS shows the generic text today NotificationService (ios/NotificationService/NotificationService.swift, §6.1.2) checks the signature, room, device, counter and index before showing text
Android app Text only for signed rows from a device the page has pinned: signed classic rows via ClassicPreview.verified, Megolm rows via MegolmKeys + MegolmPreview.verified. Unsigned, unpinned or badly signed rows show "New message" (MessageNotifier.java:347-382; ClassicPreview.java:19-20, 83-103) bridge.js hands the device's chat private key (PKCS#8) to the app via setNotifyKey, which needs the bridge token and ServerConfig.isOurs(origin) (NativeBridge.java:101-103). NotifyKeys seals it with a non-exportable Android Keystore AES key, one entry per server origin. The same key is used for inline replies, which are unsigned and disabled ("Open Twigum to reply") for any chat that has had a signed or Megolm row (NotifyActionReceiver.java:18,101; MessageNotifier.java:201-203, 264-275)
Desktop OS notifications from the page / notifiers.js Electron

5.8 What is protected and what is not (threat model)

🌱In plain words

A threat model is an honest list of who we are protecting against, what they could see, and what we can't stop. No system protects against everything. Here is what Twigum does and doesn't hide.

Protected against the server operator (and anyone with the server's disk): DM and group text, files, edited message content, key backups in v2 modes. Reaction emoji are not protected (plain text on the server, web/server.py:8177-8200). The server holds only ciphertext and wraps. This does not apply to accounts that had a v1 (legacy) key backup, until forced key rotation ships (README.md:3, web/patch-notes.html:25).

Visible to the server: who talks to whom and when (sender, conversation, ts, seq), message sizes, friend lists, group membership (group names are sealed under the group epoch key — see group_meta_refresh), display names, avatars ("The server can see this picture." — avatar_put), presence, typing, read marks, reaction emoji (stored in plain text in reactions.json, react_message), IP addresses at the network layer (not logged by the app), email addresses.

Server can read:

  • Lobby messages on public-mode servers. The client sends the message key ck so publicmode.lobby_check can open, filter and re-seal the post (web/publicmode.py line 1553).
  • v1 (legacy) key backups, which are sealed with the login password.

Visible to Apple (iOS APNs, §3.9): the sender's username in the alert ("New message from "), the top-level chat key (dm:<sender username>, g:<group id>, lobby), and for Megolm rows the m envelope (session id, ciphertext, signature, sender device id, counter, index; no plaintext) (web/server.py:8167, 1020-1029; apnspush.py:224-228, 263-276).

Defences against a malicious server inserting devices or messages: device records must be signed and bound; new keys need a fresh sign-in or password; other people pin signing keys and block changed keys until re-confirmed; message signatures cover recipients, counter and wraps; replay ledger; wrap_allowed_for_device stops a newly added device from receiving old message keys, unless another device on the same account cross-signed it (§3.4.6); the server cannot forge a signed re-wrap.

Not defended: a compromised device or browser profile; a malicious server serving modified JavaScript (the web app is delivered by the server itself — the native apps also load it from the server); metadata analysis; loss of all devices without a recovery key (old messages cannot be decrypted).

Session security: HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, HMAC-signed tokens with server-side rows, session bound to device, CSRF guard, CSP, HSTS, host check, optional TOTP, email codes for new browsers, re-auth for sensitive actions, rate limits on login and resets.

⚠️Warning: The web app comes from the server

The app's code is sent by the server each time it loads (and the phone and desktop apps load it from the server too). A server operator who changed that code could make the app leak keys. Twigum does not defend against a malicious server operator serving modified code. You are trusting whoever runs your server not to do that.

6. The phone and desktop apps (native apps)

🌱In plain words

The iPhone, Android and desktop apps are like a picture frame around the web app. The picture (the chat app) is the same everywhere and comes from your server. The frame adds the things only a real app can do: proper notifications, the "Share to Twigum" button, saving files and remembering several servers.

All native apps wrap the same web app. They never contain a second copy of the chat logic; they add platform features and keep the WebView on trusted addresses.

6.1 iPhone and iPad

Project: XcodeGen spec ios/project.yml (run xcodegen generate on a Mac to make the Xcode project). Swift 5, iOS 16.0 or newer, iPhone and iPad, no Mac Catalyst.

The app has three parts (targets): the app itself, a Notification Service extension (a tiny helper iOS runs when a notification arrives, to change its text) and a Share extension (what appears when you tap Share → Twigum in another app).

Target Bundle ID Type Sources Entitlements
Twigum app.branchchat.ios (the existing App ID; must not change so the app updates in place and keeps its keychain) application Twigum/Sources, Twigum/Resources, Shared, ShareCommon aps-environment (development in repo; distribution re-signs as production), App Group group.app.branchchat.ios
NotificationService app.branchchat.ios.NotificationService app extension NotificationService, Shared App Group group.app.branchchat.ios
ShareExtension app.branchchat.ios.share app extension ShareExtension, ShareCommon App Group group.app.branchchat.ios

DEVELOPMENT_TEAM (the Apple developer team that signs the app) is empty in the repo. MARKETING_VERSION is "26.11.1401". The build number (CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) must follow the YYYYMMDDRR rule (Start here, Version numbers).

Main app sources (ios/Twigum/Sources/):

File Role
AppDelegate.swift Asks for notification permission, registers for APNs, keeps the token (deviceTokenHex), shows banners in the foreground, forwards a tapped notification's chat to the web view (twigumOpenFromPush).
SceneDelegate.swift Creates the window and WebViewController; handles universal links (only for trusted URLs) and twigum://share; clears delivered notifications for chats read elsewhere (DeliveredChatClear).
AppConfig.swift Front door URL (TwigumServerURL in Info.plist = https://branchchat.app/; TEMPORARY, per the comment, until the branchchat.app → twigum.app session/key hand-off ships: Info.plist:30-35, AppConfig.swift:16-17, docs/TWIGUM-DOMAIN-CUTOVER.md:9-16. Do not "fix" it to twigum.app, or iOS users lose their keys and session), home hosts twigum.app, www.twigum.app, branchchat.app, www.branchchat.app; isOurs() decides which URLs stay in the app. isOurs also returns true for saved servers (AppConfig.swift:38,46), so a saved server gets the full iOS bridge and the APNs token. This is acceptable because servers only come from directory attestation or old-app storage.
WebViewController.swift The WKWebView; message handlers (§4.9); push token hand-off to the page (/api/push/apns); offline screen.
ServerStore.swift Saved servers (§6.1.1).
ShareHandoff.swift Passes shared files from the App Group inbox to the page (__bcLoadSharedFiles; message handler bcShareFiles, line 25).
DownloadHandler.swift bcSaveFile: saves files through the share sheet (§3.8).
DeliveredChatClear.swift Clears delivered notifications for chats read elsewhere.
Resources/bridge.js, composer-shim.js, share-attach.js Scripts injected into the page (WebViewController.swift:80-90); bridge.js defines BranchChatNative/TwigumNative (§4.9).

URL schemes (Info.plist): twigum, twigumdev, branchchat, branchchatdev.

6.1.1 How the iPhone app remembers servers (keychain)

The keychain is the iPhone's locked safe for passwords and keys.

ServerStore.swift keeps the list of servers and the one to reopen:

  • Keychain generic-password items, service app.branchchat.dev.ios.servers (the old BranchChat Dev app's service, kept so updated apps open the same server), accessible after first unlock, this device only. Accounts: bc.servers.known (JSON array of origins), bc.servers.names (origin → name), bc.servers.session (origin to reopen; absent = front door).
  • Read-only fallbacks if the primary item is missing: keychain service app.branchchat.ios.servers, then UserDefaults keys bc.servers.*. Values found there are copied to the primary item. Saved servers are deleted only when the person removes one; the bc.servers.session item is deleted when the person goes back to the front door (ServerStore.swift:199-203).
  • New servers are only accepted from the front door's directory (/api/directory or /api/signin-servers), exact host, port 443. Directory cache 300 s. Max 50 servers.
  • Add server on iOS loads the front door's /#own page (WebViewController.swift:522-525). A server is remembered only when navigation reaches a host the directory lists (:330-332). iOS never probes /.well-known/branchchat or /api/version; that probe is Android and desktop only.
  • Page API: bcServers → listServers, openServer, addServer, removeServer.

6.1.2 Notification Service extension

ios/NotificationService/NotificationService.swift: for a Megolm payload (m = {sid, b, sg, n, sd, i, c}) it shows decrypted text only if: the top-level chat equals m.c, the session is in MegolmKeyStore for the active server origin, and MegolmPreview.verified passes (pinned P-256 signature of the sender device, room/device/counter binding, message index). Otherwise, and on timeout, the server's text stays ("New message from {name}" / "New message"). It never logs content or keys.

ios/Shared/MegolmKeyStore.swift: one keychain item per Megolm session in access group group.app.branchchat.ios, service app.twigum.megolm.v2|<origin>, after-first-unlock-this-device-only, max 2000 sessions per server, cleared per server on sign-out (bcClearKeys). Items under the old service app.twigum.megolm.v1 are never read again.

6.1.3 Share extension

  1. The person taps Share → Twigum in another app.
  2. The Share extension copies the items into the shared App Group inbox (locked when the phone is locked; deleted after 30 minutes).
  3. It opens the main app with twigum://share.
  4. The app hands the files to the web page (ShareHandoff → __bcLoadSharedFiles, token-checked).
  5. The person picks a chat and sends; the page locks and uploads as usual (§3.8).

ShareExtension copies shared photos/files/text into the App Group inbox (ShareCommon/ShareInbox.swift, file protection complete, 30-minute lifetime), then opens twigum://share. The app's ShareHandoff gives them to the page through the injected native script share-attach.js (ios/Twigum/Resources/) and the page's share-picker.js, which checks a token. No network or keychain in the extension.

6.2 Android

Item Value Source
Package app.branchchat.android (debug: .debug) android/app/build.gradle
SDK minSdk 26, compileSdk/targetSdk 36 build.gradle
Language Java; AndroidX webkit + core only android/README.md
Front door branchchatServerUrl=https://twigum.app/ → BuildConfig.DEFAULT_SERVER_URL; branchchat.app also trusted android/gradle.properties, ServerConfig.java
Version versionName = VERSION; versionCode computed in build.gradle (§7.1)
Release R8 + resource shrinking; signed AAB (Play) and APK (sideload) via build-release.sh

Main classes (android/app/src/main/java/app/branchchat/android/): MainActivity (WebView, navigation, insets, back, pickers, permissions, offline screen), ServerConfig (the one place that decides trusted origins; probes new servers; reopens the last verified server), NativeBridge (token-guarded @JavascriptInterface, §4.9), MessageNotifier + PushService (notifications), NotifyKeys (Keystore-sealed device keys), MegolmPreview / ClassicPreview / E2ECrypto (decrypt previews), ConvNotifications, Updater (in-app update check), SharedMedia, DownloadSaver.

Notifications without FCM. Web Push does not work inside an Android WebView. MessageNotifier long-polls the server with the WebView's own session cookie. PushService is a foreground service (type remoteMessaging, a silent minimum-importance "Sync" notification) so the long-poll keeps network access in Doze and is not frozen. A JobScheduler job (every 15 minutes) covers the case where the process is gone. No Google account or FCM. Notification text is decrypted on the phone with the key from NotifyKeys.

Security: the bridge is injected only into trusted origins, every bridge call needs a per-launch random token, other origins open externally, no cleartext, Safe Browsing on, no cloud backup of WebView data (data_extraction_rules.xml).

📘Good To Know: Why Android shows a "Sync" notification

Android stops background apps from using the network to save battery. To keep receiving messages without Google's push service, the Twigum app runs a foreground service, which Android only allows if the app shows a notification. That is the quiet, minimum-importance "Sync" notification. You can hide it in Android's notification settings for the Twigum app; messages still arrive.

6.3 Desktop (Windows and Linux)

Electron is a kit that wraps a web app in a desktop window, using the same engine as the Chrome browser.

Item Value
App id app.branchchat.desktop (Flatpak app.branchchat.Desktop)
Front door DEFAULT_SERVER = 'https://twigum.app/' (main.js:15); other trusted front doors (the code's LEGACY_FRONT_DOORS set): branchchat.app, www.branchchat.app, twigum.app, www.twigum.app; --front-door= for testing. The header comment at main.js:3 still says "Every launch opens the front door, https://branchchat.app/" (stale, Q7). Plain http is allowed for *.lan, *.internal, localhost and private ranges; hand-offs still need https (main.js:61-62)
Packages Linux: AppImage, deb, rpm, tar.gz (x64 + arm64); Windows: nsis, msi (x64), plus dist:win:arm64 (nsis); macOS: npm run dist:mac (dmg) is configured but has never been built or tested (desktop/package.json; BUILD.md:30-32; Q14)
Security contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, sandbox: true, navigation outside trusted servers blocked, new windows denied, external links via shell.openExternal, DevTools off in release (BC_DEVTOOLS=1 to enable)

Files main.js, preload.js, servers-model.js (pure helpers: per-origin notifier credentials, rename changes label only), ui/servers.*, updater.js, version.js (comparator), version-sync.js, notifiers.js, flatpak/, BUILD.md

Removing a server clears that server's cookies and local keys on the computer (desktop/README.md).

6.4 Switching servers on any platform

  1. The person opens the Servers menu and chooses Add or Switch.
  2. The page asks the native app (listServers, addServer, openServer).
  3. Adding on iPhone/iPad: the app shows the front door's server list; a server is saved only if it is listed (§1.4).
  4. Adding on Android/desktop: the app checks the server itself (/.well-known/branchchat or /api/version).
  5. The app saves the server and makes it the one to reopen.
  6. It loads https://<server>/. Cookies and keys are kept separately for each address, so each server has its own sign-in and device keys.

7. Run your own server

🌱In plain words

Running your own Twigum server means one computer you control (a Raspberry Pi, an old PC, or a small rented server on the internet) keeps your group's locked messages and files. You install it once with a setup script that asks six questions. After that it mostly looks after itself: it backs itself up every night and you update it with one command when a new version comes out.

This chapter follows the order you will actually do things in:

7.1 Before you start

What you need

Minimum Recommended
Computer Any 64-bit Linux computer (older Pis should work for a few people, untested) Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 (2 GB RAM or more), or any small PC or virtual machine
Operating system Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit), Debian 11+, Ubuntu 22.04+ Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (Bookworm) or Debian 12
Storage 8 GB SD card USB SSD, or a good A2 SD card. Photos and files people share are stored here (locked).
Python 3.9+ (the installer installs it) 3.11+
Network Internet access for the tunnel and email Wired Ethernet
To be reachable from anywhere A domain name on Cloudflare (free plan is fine)

(From docs/self-hosting.md. Fedora, RHEL, Rocky and Alma are described in docs/server/fedora-rhel.md but not yet tested on real machines. Docker Desktop on Windows and macOS is described in docs/server/docker-desktop.md but also not yet tested.)

📘Good To Know: Why HTTPS is required

Browsers only allow the encryption keys, notifications and "install as an app" on HTTPS pages (or on localhost). Every way of reaching the server in §7.4 gives you HTTPS. A plain http:// address will load, but the app cannot work properly on it.

Words you will meet

  • Terminal: a window where you type commands. On the server itself, or from another computer over SSH (ssh you@server-address, a secure remote terminal).
  • sudo: "do this as the administrator". It asks for your password.
  • Domain name: a name like example.com that you rent from a registrar. chat.example.com is a subdomain of it.
  • DNS: the internet's phone book that turns chat.example.com into an address computers can reach.
  • Port: a numbered door on a computer. Twigum listens on port 8766 on the server itself; people reach it on the normal HTTPS port 443 through the tunnel or proxy.
  • Reverse proxy: a program in front of Twigum that handles HTTPS and passes requests on (Caddy, nginx, Traefik, or Cloudflare's tunnel).
💡Tip: Use a dedicated machine

Use a computer or virtual machine that does nothing else important. For example, on Proxmox, run Twigum in its own small VM and never on the Proxmox host itself (docs/server/proxmox.md).

7.2 Getting the server software

There are three ways. All end with the same folder containing web/ and server/install.sh.

Server packages for 26.11.1401 are published at https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/tag/server-v26.11.1401. They are pinned to that tag; /releases/latest is used by the app updaters and will not resolve these files. In the commands below, twigum-server-install.tar.gz is the same file as branch-chat-server-26.11.1401-install.tar.gz, and twigum-server-docker-compose.tar.gz is the same file as branch-chat-server-26.11.1401-docker-compose.tar.gz. The installer script is also published on its own as https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/download/server-v26.11.1401/install.sh (the same file as server/install.sh inside the package). Run it from the unpacked tree; it needs the rest of the package.

Option A: a release package (easiest)

  1. On the server, download the install package and the checksum file:

    curl -fLO https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/download/server-v26.11.1401/twigum-server-install.tar.gz
curl -fLO https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/download/server-v26.11.1401/SHA256SUMS

  2. Check the download: grep 'twigum-server-install.tar.gz$' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c. You should see twigum-server-install.tar.gz: OK.

  3. Unpack it: tar -xzf twigum-server-install.tar.gz
  4. Go into the folder it made: cd branch-chat-server-*. It contains web/, server/, VERSION and docs/.

Option B: the source package (or git, for team members with repository access only)

The public way to build from source is the source package on the same release:

curl -fLO https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/download/server-v26.11.1401/branch-chat-26.11.1401-source.tar.gz
curl -fLO https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/download/server-v26.11.1401/SHA256SUMS
grep 'branch-chat-26.11.1401-source.tar.gz$' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c
tar -xzf branch-chat-26.11.1401-source.tar.gz
cd branch-chat-26.11.1401-source
sudo ./server/install.sh

The Twigum git repository (NexusMcNexis/twigum) is private. A git clone only works if you already have access (SSH: git@github.com:NexusMcNexis/twigum.git). Team members can then run sudo ./server/install.sh from the clone. To install a specific release, check out that release branch (for this cut, release/26.11.1401) before running the installer. Updates of a git install use git pull --ff-only automatically (§7.10).

Option C: build the package yourself (from any copy of the source with git history)

tools/make-server-release.sh [ref] [outdir] builds the packages from a committed version only (no untracked files, no local settings, no data):

cd twigum                                   # your copy of the source
bash tools/make-server-release.sh HEAD dist-release
ls dist-release

You should see branch-chat-server-<version>-install.tar.gz, branch-chat-server-<version>-docker-compose.tar.gz, branch-chat-<version>-source.tar.gz, RELEASE-NOTES-server.md and SHA256SUMS (that is what the script writes; the published GitHub release also adds the version-less twigum-server-* names, branch-chat-server-latest-install.tar.gz, a standalone install.sh, and a SHA256SUMS that covers those aliases too). Copy the install package to the server and continue with Option A, step 3.

7.3 Installing with the setup wizard

🛠️Step by step: Run the setup wizard

Where: on the server, inside the unpacked folder (bash), as a user that can use sudo.

What it does: asks six questions, installs what is needed, creates a locked-down system user branchchat, writes /etc/branch-chat/config.env, starts the server, checks /healthz, creates your admin account and turns on nightly backups. Running it again later is safe: it keeps your data and your previous answers, and backs up first.

  1. Start it:

    sudo ./server/install.sh

    You see Twigum Server setup and "Press Enter to keep the value in [brackets]".

  2. 1/6 Install method: type native (a system service; lightest, best on a Pi) or docker. Press Enter for the default native.

  3. 2/6 Your group: the group or family name (one line, 60 characters or fewer; shown in page titles, the home-screen app name and invite emails), an optional accent colour like #3c92ea, and an optional background picture (.jpg, .png or .webp, 8 MB or smaller).
  4. 3/6 Admin account (you): a username (3 to 32 letters, numbers, dots or dashes), your email (sign-in codes go here) and a password typed twice (it does not show while you type). Use 12 characters or more: that is the server's default minimum (BC_MIN_PASSWORD_LEN). You become the owner.
  5. 4/6 Access: tunnel, lan or local. See §7.4 before you answer; for tunnel it also asks for your host name (for example chat.example.com) and the tunnel token.
  6. 5/6 Email: smtp (then the mail server details and password) or log. See §7.5.
  7. 6/6 Backups: how many nightly backups to keep (default 14).
  8. It shows a Summary line and installs. Each stage starts with ==>, and each success shows ok.
  9. You should see "Twigum Server is set up." followed by your next step (for tunnel, the exact hostname and service to enter in Cloudflare; see §7.4).

Check it worked:

sudo ./server/install.sh status

You should see mode: native access: tunnel port: 8766, the config and data paths, the code folder with its version, the service shown as active (running), health: ok, and the latest backup.

If it fails: the installer stops with error: … and the line it failed at, and writes details to /var/log/branch-chat-install.log. Nothing is deleted. Fix the cause (the message says what: for example "enter a real email address", or "this machine already has a docker install") and run it again. To read the full log: sudo less /var/log/branch-chat-install.log (press q to leave).

7.4 How people reach your server (access modes)

Mode Who can reach it You need Good for
tunnel (recommended) Anyone with the address, from anywhere A domain on Cloudflare (free plan) Most families and groups. No router changes; your home IP address stays hidden.
lan Only devices on your home network Nothing extra, but each device must trust a certificate once A household that only chats at home
local Only the server itself, until you put something in front Your own reverse proxy or VPN People who already run nginx, Caddy, Traefik or Tailscale
🛠️Step by step: Set up a Cloudflare Tunnel (access "tunnel")

What it does: the server makes an outgoing connection to Cloudflare, and Cloudflare serves your address over HTTPS. No ports are opened on your router.

  1. Add your domain to Cloudflare (the free plan is fine).
  2. In the Cloudflare dashboard go to Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel, choose Cloudflared, give it a name (for example branch-chat), and copy the token: the long string after --token in the install command Cloudflare shows. You do not need to run Cloudflare's command.
  3. Run the installer, choose access tunnel, enter your host name (for example chat.example.com) and paste the token. The installer stores it in a file only root can read (/etc/branch-chat/secrets/), installs cloudflared and starts the branch-chat-tunnel service.
  4. Back in the tunnel's Public hostnames tab, add: hostname chat.example.com, service http://localhost:8766 (native) or http://branch-chat:8766 (Docker). The installer's last message prints exactly these values.
  5. Check: open https://chat.example.com. You should see the Twigum sign-in page. curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version should print the version.
  6. If it fails: an error page with 502 or 1033 means the tunnel can't reach Twigum. Check the service URL in step 4, then sudo systemctl status branch-chat-tunnel (Docker: sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml -p branch-chat logs cloudflared).
📘Good To Know: Large files and Cloudflare

Cloudflare's free plan limits one request to 100 MB. Twigum already uploads big files in 8 MB pieces (§3.8), so this does not matter.

🛠️Step by step: Home network only (access "lan")

What it does: installs the Caddy web server with its own private certificate authority (a mini "ID card office" that only your devices trust), serving https://<name>.local and https://<the server's IP address>. Nothing is reachable from the internet.

  1. Run the installer and choose access lan.
  2. Each phone or computer must trust Caddy's root certificate once, or the browser warns and the encryption features do not work. Print it on the server:
    • Native: sudo cat /var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt
    • Docker: sudo cat /opt/branch-chat/caddy-data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt
  3. Copy that file to each device and install it:
    • Android: Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate.
    • iPhone/iPad: open the file, install the profile, then turn it on in Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.
    • Computer: import it into the browser's or the system's certificate store as a trusted root.
  4. Check: open https://<name>.local (or https://<IP address>) on that device. There should be no certificate warning.
  5. If it fails: .local names need mDNS (Raspberry Pi OS has it); otherwise use the IP address. On Fedora/RHEL the firewall must allow HTTPS: sudo firewall-cmd --add-service=https --permanent && sudo firewall-cmd --reload.
🛠️Step by step: Bring your own proxy (access "local")

What it does: Twigum listens only on 127.0.0.1:8766; you put your own HTTPS reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, Traefik) or VPN in front.

  1. Run the installer, choose access local, and give the public host name so links in emails are right.
  2. Point your proxy at http://127.0.0.1:8766 and forward the Host header unchanged (Twigum refuses names it doesn't know, §3.2).
  3. If your proxy talks to Twigum from another machine, list it in BC_TRUSTED_PROXIES so its "this came in over http/https" header is believed (Appendix B).
  4. On a rented server, open only ports 80 and 443: sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp.
  5. Tailscale alternative: choose local and run tailscale serve --bg 8766 to get a trusted HTTPS address on your tailnet.
  6. Check: curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version. If it fails with That page was not found., the Host header is not passed through or the name is not in BC_PUBLIC_URL/BC_HOSTS.

7.5 Email

New devices confirm sign-in with a 6-digit code sent by email; invites and password resets are emailed too.

  • smtp (recommended): any email provider works (your internet provider, Fastmail, Proton Bridge, Mailgun, Gmail with an app password, …). Port 587 uses STARTTLS; port 465 uses TLS. The password is stored in /etc/branch-chat/secrets/smtp_password (readable only by root and the service), never in config.env.
  • log: nothing is emailed; codes and invite links are written to the server log. The admin reads them with sudo ./server/install.sh logs and passes them on. Good for testing, or a household where the admin is always around.
💡Tip: Test your email

After installing with smtp, sign out and sign in from a private browser window. If the code arrives within a minute, email works. If not, check the SMTP settings in /etc/branch-chat/config.env (BC_SMTP_HOST, BC_SMTP_PORT, BC_SMTP_USER, BC_SMTP_TLS) and look for mail errors in sudo ./server/install.sh logs.

7.6 Installing without questions (non-interactive)

Every question has a flag (sudo ./server/install.sh --help lists them). Useful for scripts and for re-creating a server.

printf '%s\n' 'a-long-admin-password' | sudo tee /root/bc-admin-pw >/dev/null; sudo chmod 600 /root/bc-admin-pw
sudo ./server/install.sh -y --mode native --name "The Smith Family" \
  --admin sam --admin-email sam@example.com --admin-password-file /root/bc-admin-pw \
  --access tunnel --hostname chat.example.com --tunnel-token-file /root/cf-token \
  --mail smtp --mail-from "Smith Family Chat <chat@example.com>" \
  --smtp-host smtp.example.com --smtp-port 587 --smtp-user chat@example.com --smtp-password-file /root/smtp-pw
sudo shred -u /root/bc-admin-pw

(From docs/self-hosting.md. The backslash \ at the end of a line means "the command continues on the next line".)

Flag Meaning
-y, --non-interactive Never ask; use the flags, then the existing settings, then defaults
--mode native\|docker System service (default) or Docker Compose
--name NAME Group or family name
--admin USER, --admin-email EMAIL Owner username and email
--admin-password-file FILE File holding the admin password (or set BC_ADMIN_PASSWORD)
--accent '#rrggbb', --background FILE Accent colour, background picture
--access tunnel\|lan\|local, --hostname HOST How people reach it, and its name
--tunnel-token-file FILE Cloudflare Tunnel token (or set BC_TUNNEL_TOKEN)
--mail smtp\|log, --mail-from 'Name <addr>' Email mode and sender
--smtp-host H --smtp-port P --smtp-user U --smtp-tls starttls\|ssl\|none SMTP server
--smtp-password-file FILE SMTP password file (or set BC_SMTP_PASSWORD)
--port N Local port (default 8766)
--keep N Nightly backups to keep (default 14)
--skip-packages Don't install system packages (they must already be there)
⚠️Warning: Keep passwords out of your shell history

Pass passwords in files (--admin-password-file, --smtp-password-file, --tunnel-token-file) with mode 600, as above, and delete them afterwards with shred -u. Typing a password directly into a command line saves it in your shell history.

7.7 Docker

The same image runs on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5 with a 64-bit OS, most servers). The easiest way is still the installer with --mode docker: it installs Docker Engine from Docker's official repository if needed, builds the image, writes /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml and sets up backups.

🛠️Step by step: Run with Docker Compose by hand

Where: on the server, in the server/ folder of the source or of the docker-compose package (bash).

  1. Make your settings file, readable only by you:

    cp config.env.example config.env && chmod 600 config.env

    Edit it (nano config.env): set at least BC_PUBLIC_URL, BC_INSTANCE_NAME, BC_OWNER and the mail settings. For a first try, BC_MAIL_MODE=log. For SMTP in Docker, use BC_SMTP_PASSWORD in config.env, or mount a file and point BC_SMTP_PASSWORD_FILE at it.

  2. Make the data folder, owned by the container's user (id 10001):

    mkdir -p data && sudo chown 10001:10001 data && chmod 700 data

  3. Build the image: docker compose build (a few minutes the first time, longer on a Pi).

  4. Create your admin account:

    docker compose run --rm branch-chat python manage.py create-admin --username sam --email sam@example.com

  5. Start it: docker compose up -d

  6. Check: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8766/healthz prints ok.
  7. With a Cloudflare Tunnel: put TUNNEL_TOKEN=... in server/.env (chmod 600 .env), then docker compose --profile tunnel up -d.
  8. If it fails: docker compose logs --tail 100 branch-chat. A "permission denied" on /data means step 2 was skipped.

What the compose file sets up (server/docker-compose.yml): service branch-chat with env_file: ./config.env; inside the container BC_HOST=0.0.0.0, BC_PORT=8766, BC_STATE_DIR=/data, BC_APP_DIR=/app; the port published as ${BC_PUBLISH:-127.0.0.1:8766} (only on the server itself unless you change BC_PUBLISH); the data volume ${BC_DATA:-./data}:/data; a read-only root file system; all extra powers dropped; a health check on /healthz. The optional cloudflared service starts only with --profile tunnel. Nothing secret is baked into the image.

⚠️Warning: One container per data folder

Run exactly one Twigum container (or service) per data folder. Two programs writing the same files will corrupt them.

7.8 First sign-in, inviting people and the Administrator page

  1. Open your address (for example https://chat.example.com) and sign in with the admin account. If this browser is new, a 6-digit code is emailed to you (in log mode: sudo ./server/install.sh logs).
  2. The app shows your recovery key for the key backup (§5.6). Write it down and keep it somewhere safe.
  3. Invite people from the menu (Invite friend or family / Create invite link). Share the link or show the QR code. Each link works once, for 72 hours (§3.6).
  4. From the command line, manage.py invite --email <address> prints an invite link too (§7.12).

The Administrator page. The owner account (BC_OWNER) gets an Administrator entry at the bottom of the profile menu. It opens /admin, which nobody else can load (others get "not found"). It asks the owner to confirm it's them first (password, then the authenticator code if two-factor is on, then an emailed code if this browser was never verified; or approval from another signed-in device). The admin session lasts 15 minutes. The page holds:

  • account and invite tools;
  • the directory listing status, with pause and resume (§7.9);
  • version and update information;
  • report and filter tools on public servers;
  • every setting in the settings file. Changes are staged until Apply, which checks every value, keeps a dated copy of the old file in config-backups/, writes the new file and restarts the server; if the server can't start, it restores the old file. Secrets (anything named like a password, token or key) are never sent to the browser; they can only be replaced or removed. Listen address and port, data and program folders are shown but locked: edit those by hand.
📘Good To Know: Docker and the Administrator page

In Docker, settings in the env_file win and are shown locked; the page saves its changes to config.env in the data folder. On native installs, config.env is 660 root:branchchat and the service is allowed to write only that file, so Apply works.

7.9 Listing your server in the public directory (optional)

This is how your server talks to the public front door. §3.14 explains exactly what is sent; in short, only your address, the time and a signature, every 5 minutes.

🛠️Step by step: Turn on the directory listing

Where: on the server (bash), or the Administrator page.

  1. Decide the name and picture people will see. Add to /etc/branch-chat/config.env (or set on the Administrator page):

    BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=1
BC_ORG_NAME=The Smith Family
BC_ORG_TYPE=family

    Optional: BC_ORG_ICON=/var/lib/branch-chat/branding/crest.webp (PNG, JPEG or WebP, 64 KB max). BC_ORG_TYPE can be family, church, school, club, business or community.

  2. Make sure the server's clock is right (pings more than 120 s off are refused): timedatectl should say System clock synchronized: yes. If not: sudo timedatectl set-ntp true.

  3. Restart: sudo systemctl restart branch-chat (Docker: sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml -p branch-chat up -d).
  4. Check: run directory-status (§3.14). Within about 5 minutes last ping: shows a time and no error. Then open https://twigum.app/directory and look for your name.
  5. If it fails:
    • Your server is on a private address (home network only, lan mode): the front door can't check it, so the listing stays pending until the front door's operator vouches for it. The directory is meant for servers reachable from the internet.
    • 409 in the last ping message: another key is listed live for your address (for example after a reinstall). Wait 15 minutes, or restore server-identity.json from a backup.
  6. To stop being listed: set BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=0 and restart (the listing disappears 15 minutes after the last ping), or pause it for a while with directory-pause --minutes N or the Administrator page.
📘Good To Know: Invite links use the front door even when you are not listed

Since 26.10.10 invite links open through https://twigum.app/join?... whether or not you are listed. The secret token stays after the # and is never sent to twigum.app; people still choose their password on your server. If you'd rather not use the front door at all for invites, set BC_INVITE_DIRECT=1 (§3.14). The code comment explains why links go through the front door: the Twigum Android app verifies only the front door's links, so it can catch invites for every server that way (web/directory.py invite_link).

7.10 Updating

🛠️Step by step: Update to a newer version

Where: on the server (bash), in the folder you installed from.

  1. Get the new code. Git install: nothing to do (the update runs git pull --ff-only; if you checked out a tag, run git checkout main or the newer tag first). Package install: download and unpack the newer package (§7.2), then cd into the new folder.
  2. Optional, for virtual machines: take a snapshot first (for example in Proxmox), so you can roll back the whole machine.

  3. Run:

    sudo ./server/install.sh update

  4. What it does: makes a backup (stops if the backup fails, changing nothing) → installs the new code next to the old (native: a new folder in /opt/branch-chat/releases/; Docker: a new image, keeping the old one as branch-chat:previous) → runs manage.py migrate → restarts → waits for /healthz.

  5. You should see ok updated and healthy.
  6. Check: sudo ./server/install.sh status shows the new version, and curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version agrees. Open the app; it reloads itself with the new code (§4.7).
  7. If it fails: the update rolls back automatically and says "update failed and was rolled back". Read the reason with sudo journalctl -u branch-chat -n 80 (Docker: sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml logs). Your data was backed up in step 4 and is unchanged.
📘Good To Know: Apps and servers must share the same YY.MM

An app and a server work together when the first two parts of their versions (YY.MM, for example 26.11) match (/api/version → api, min_app). Keep your server updated so people's phone apps keep working after they update.

7.11 Backups and restoring

🌱In plain words

A backup is a copy of everything kept somewhere safe, so that if the server's disk breaks you can put it all back. Twigum makes one every night by itself. But a backup on the same disk dies with that disk, so copy backups to another place now and then.

Nightly backups run at about 03:30 (systemd timer branch-chat-backup.timer) into /var/backups/branch-chat/ as branch-chat-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.tar.gz (mode 600), keeping the newest 14 (or what you chose). Each contains the data folder and /etc/branch-chat (including secrets). A backup is skipped (and the job fails) when free space is low. The unfinished-upload folder is left out.

🛠️Step by step: Back up now and copy backups off the server

Where: on the server (bash).

  1. Back up now: sudo ./server/install.sh backup
  2. Check: sudo ls -lh /var/backups/branch-chat/ lists a new branch-chat-<date>-<time>.tar.gz.

  3. Copy all backups to another disk, for example a USB drive mounted at /mnt/usb:

    sudo rsync -a /var/backups/branch-chat/ /mnt/usb/branch-chat-backups/

  4. If it fails: "free space is low" means the disk is nearly full: delete old files you don't need, or lower the number kept (--keep, re-run the installer).

⚠️Warning: Backups are sensitive

Messages and files in backups are locked, but account data, key backups (locked), email addresses and the server's secrets (session.key, the push key, server-identity.json, the SMTP password and tunnel token) are in there too. Keep backups as private as the server itself.

🛠️Step by step: Restore a backup

Where: on the server (bash), in the folder you installed from.

  1. Pick the backup: sudo ls -1t /var/backups/branch-chat/ (newest first).

  2. Restore it:

    sudo ./server/install.sh restore /var/backups/branch-chat/branch-chat-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.tar.gz

  3. It asks "Replace the current data …? [y/N]". Type y and press Enter.

  4. What it does: checks the file really is a Twigum backup → stops the server → moves the current data aside to /var/lib/branch-chat.before-restore-<time> (nothing is deleted) → unpacks the backup → fixes ownership → starts the server → waits for /healthz.
  5. You should see ok restored and healthy.
  6. Good to know: settings in the backup (/etc/branch-chat) are not restored automatically; extract them by hand if you need them, for example on a brand-new machine: sudo tar -C / -xzf <backup> etc/branch-chat.
  7. If it fails: the old data is still in /var/lib/branch-chat.before-restore-<time>. Read the log (sudo ./server/install.sh logs).

7.12 Admin commands (manage.py)

manage.py is a small command-line tool for jobs that are easier without the web page. Run it with the same settings as the server:

  • Native:

    sudo -u branchchat BC_CONFIG=/etc/branch-chat/config.env BC_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/branch-chat \
  python3 /opt/branch-chat/app/manage.py status

  • Docker (installer):

    sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml -p branch-chat exec branch-chat python manage.py status

Replace status with the command you need:

Command What it does
status Shows the config file, data and program folders, listen address, public URL, host names, name, owner, mail mode, data-format version, and the number of accounts, admins and pending invites
healthcheck Asks /healthz; used by Docker's health check
create-admin --username U --email E [--password-stdin] [--reset-password] Creates the first admin (safe to repeat). The password comes from standard input, $BC_ADMIN_PASSWORD, or a prompt
set-password --username U [--password-stdin] Sets a person's password
user-exists --username U Checks whether an account exists
invite --email E [--role member\|admin] [--invited-by U] Creates an invite and prints the link
settle-invites [--apply] Tidies old invites (without --apply it only shows what it would do)
set-staff-label --username U (--label "AI assistant"\|"Bot" \| --clear) Marks an account as an AI assistant or bot, or clears it
migrate Upgrades the data format (the updater runs it for you)
directory-status, directory-ping [--offline], directory-pause --minutes N, directory-resume Your directory listing (§3.14, §7.9)

The other directory-* commands (directory-list, -hide, -ban, -vouch, -pin, -revoke and their opposites, directory-forget, directory-admin-tls) are for the operator of a front door (BC_HOME_MODE=1) and do nothing useful on an ordinary server.

⚠️Warning: Stop the server before changing accounts from the command line

Stop the server before create-admin or set-password (sudo systemctl stop branch-chat, then start it again afterwards), or use the web page instead. The running server keeps accounts in memory and could overwrite your change.

7.13 Uninstalling

  • Remove the program but keep your data: sudo ./server/install.sh uninstall. It removes the services and code and keeps the data (/var/lib/branch-chat), backups (/var/backups/branch-chat) and settings (/etc/branch-chat/config.env).
  • Remove everything, including data and backups: sudo ./server/install.sh uninstall --purge.
⚠️Warning: --purge cannot be undone

--purge deletes every message, file, account and backup on the server. Copy a backup somewhere else first if there is any chance you will want it.

7.14 Keeping it safe (hardening checklist)

  • The native service runs as its own branchchat user with systemd sandboxing: NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, no capabilities, limited network types, writable only in its data folder. (systemd-analyze security branch-chat scores about 3.0 "OK".)
  • The tunnel token is readable only by root; the SMTP password only by root and the service.
  • The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only; only the tunnel or Caddy faces the network.
  • Keep the operating system updated: sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade; consider unattended-upgrades.
  • Turn on two-factor (an authenticator app) for the owner account.
  • Copy backups off the server regularly (§7.11) and keep them private.
  • Don't copy the data folder while the server is writing; use the backup command.
  • Leave BC_VODOZEMAC off (§5.5): it is experimental.

8. Everyday checks

🌱In plain words

A server is like a car: most days you just use it, but now and then you glance at the dashboard. These are the dashboard lights: is it up, is it the right version, is the disk filling up, did last night's backup happen?

Check Command (on the server, bash) Healthy answer
Everything at once sudo ./server/install.sh status (from the folder you installed from) active (running) (native) or the container Up (Docker), health: ok, and a recent latest backup
Version from outside curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/version (any computer) the version you installed
Log sudo ./server/install.sh logs no Traceback lines
Free disk df -h /var/lib/branch-chat plenty free; uploads stop below 1 GiB free (FREE_FLOOR)
Backups sudo ls -lh /var/backups/branch-chat/ one file per night, newest from last night
Backup timer systemctl list-timers branch-chat-backup.timer a NEXT time tonight around 03:30
Directory (if listed) manage.py directory-status (§3.14) last ping within the last 5 minutes, no error
💡Tip: Storage budget

The server stops accepting uploads when stored files reach BC_STORE_BUDGET_GB (default 10 GB) or free disk falls below 1 GiB. When space runs short, the oldest videos are removed first ("This video expired to free space."); photos and other files are never removed automatically. Raise BC_STORE_BUDGET_GB if your disk is bigger. /api/version shows the current store_budget in bytes.

9. Troubleshooting

🌱In plain words

When something goes wrong, work like a detective: first find out where the problem is (the person's device, the network, or the server), then read the exact message, then look it up below. Most messages in Twigum are written to tell you what to do next.

9.1 First steps for any problem

🛠️Step by step: Narrow it down
  1. Is the server up? From any computer: curl -s https://chat.example.com/api/health. Healthy: {"ok": true}. If nothing comes back, or an error page: the server or the tunnel/proxy is down (§9.3).
  2. Is it one person or everyone? If only one person has the problem, it is almost always their device or app (§9.2). If everyone does, it is the server (§9.3).
  3. Read the exact words of the message on screen and find them in the tables below.
  4. Check the server log (§3.13) around the time it happened.
  5. Still stuck? Ask the person to use Report a bug in the app (§3.10): it sends the steps, screenshots and app details (no logs, no message content).

9.2 Messages people see in the app

Symptom Likely cause What to check / do
"Reload Twigum to send this message." 422 sign_required: an old page without signing tried to send from a device that has published a signing key. The same text comes with 422 ctr_reused (web/server.py:1157, 1196-1197, 8651-8652), but the client retries ctr_reused once by itself (app.js:2288-2292), so the text usually means sign_required Reload; check the service worker updated (bc-sw-updated)
Send fails once then works 422 ctr_reused; client retried with a higher counter Normal. Repeated failures: check IndexedDB send-counter:* and clock
"Turn on message signing": "This device needs to confirm your signing key before it can send messages. Type your password." (with TOTP: "…password and a current authenticator or backup code.") The signing-unlock page; this device must confirm its signing key (not the 422) (app.js:1089-1092, 1126-1132) Type the password (and code)
"Wait a second and try again." / 429 More than one post per second (too_fast) or group action too fast Slow down
"Sign in again." after opening the app Session bound to another device (bind_session_device) Sign in again; keys and history stay
"Too many devices": "This account already has 8 devices with message keys. Remove one to continue on this device." (after 409 too_many_devices) 8 device keys, none unused for 30 days (web/server.py:6897-6902) Remove a device; Remove asks "Type your password to remove this device's message key." (app.js:24935, 24954, 25077)
"…'s device key changed. Messages from it are blocked until you re-confirm." Friend reinstalled or the key really changed Verify with the friend (safety number), then re-confirm. Key pins live only on each person's own device (IndexedDB); the server and the team can't clear this warning. Re-confirming keeps the old key as previous, so earlier messages still verify (app.js:1876-1894; crypto.js:890-901)
"This message was rejected (replay).", "(signature missing)." (unsigned), "(old encryption in a chat that moved to the new one)." (downgrade), "(signature)." (anything else) Failed verification (app.js:2465-2473) Do not trust the message; report with a bug report
Old messages show as locked on a new device No key backup restored / device not approved Restore with the recovery key; or approve from an old device
"This video expired to free space." (410, expired: true) Evicted by evict_old_videos (storage budget or free disk short) (web/server.py:2325, 9500; app.js:12328) Raise BC_STORE_BUDGET_GB or accept
"This video is too large to play here. Use Save to keep it." Video over 80 MiB (INLINE_VIDEO_MAX), or unknown size with no local copy Save it (§3.8)
Upload refused Over file_max, store budget, or disk under 1 GiB free /api/version shows file_max, store_budget; check disk
iPhone web push stops Safari cancels subscriptions whose pushes show nothing Placeholder logic in sw.js; reopen the app to resubscribe
iOS notification shows "New message from …" only Not Megolm (always the case while BC_VODOZEMAC=0), NSE has no session key, or a check failed Expected today
Android notifications late Doze / battery optimisation; PushService not running Check the "Sync" notification exists; allow background use
iOS app opens the wrong server ServerStore session value Servers menu; keychain service app.branchchat.dev.ios.servers
📘Good To Know: Key-change warnings can only be cleared by a person

Key pins live only on each person's own device. If someone sees "…'s device key changed", neither the server admin nor the developers can clear it for them. The safe fix is to check with the friend (in person or by phone) that they really reinstalled or got a new device, compare the safety number, and then tap re-confirm.

9.3 Server problems

Symptom Likely cause What to do
/healthz does not answer The Twigum program is not running sudo ./server/install.sh status, then sudo ./server/install.sh logs (native: sudo journalctl -u branch-chat -n 80). Fix the error shown, then sudo systemctl restart branch-chat.
"That page was not found." for every page The address in the browser is not BC_PUBLIC_URL's host and not in BC_HOSTS Fix BC_PUBLIC_URL or add the name to BC_HOSTS (§3.11), restart. With your own proxy, pass the Host header through unchanged.
Sign-in asks for a code that never arrives Email settings wrong Check the SMTP settings (§7.5), or switch to log mode and read the code with sudo ./server/install.sh logs.
Browser warns about the certificate (LAN mode) The device does not trust Caddy's root certificate Install it on that device (§7.4).
Tunnel shows 502 or 1033 Cloudflare can't reach Twigum Check the public hostname's service URL in Cloudflare (http://localhost:8766 native, http://branch-chat:8766 Docker), then sudo systemctl status branch-chat-tunnel (Docker: … logs cloudflared).
Uploads refused File over file_max, storage budget reached, or disk under 1 GiB free /api/version shows file_max and store_budget; df -h /var/lib/branch-chat.
Administrator Apply broke the server A bad setting The server restores the previous file by itself on the next start (adminpage.recover_after_failed_start); older copies are in config-backups/.
Update failed The new version did not start The updater rolled back already (§7.10); read sudo journalctl -u branch-chat -n 80.
Container unhealthy (Docker) manage.py healthcheck → /healthz fails sudo docker compose -f /opt/branch-chat/docker-compose.yml -p branch-chat logs --tail 100 branch-chat; manage.py status.
Not shown in the directory Reporting off, clock wrong, private address, or a key clash §7.9 step 5.
App stuck on an old version after an update The browser still runs the old copy of the app Close every Twigum tab and open it again (or pull to refresh in the app). The service worker swaps in the new copy and reloads (§4.7).
iPhone app won't save the server Not listed in the front door's directory, or not on port 443, or an internationalised name List the server (§7.9) on port 443 with a plain ASCII name.

10. Glossary (word list)

Each word has a plain explanation first, then the exact meaning in Twigum where that matters.

Word In plain words In Twigum
AAD (additional authenticated data) Extra words glued to a locked message so it can't be moved to another chat without the lock noticing. Sender device, chat and counter bound into AES-GCM ("twigum-msg-aad-v1", §5.1).
Admin / owner The person in charge of a server. The owner is the account named in BC_OWNER; only it can open the Administrator page (/admin). Admins can manage people.
Administrator page The server's settings screen, in the app. /admin, owner only; edits config.env with Apply (§7.8, §3.11).
AES-GCM A strong, fast padlock that also notices if anyone tampered with what's inside. AES-256-GCM for messages, wraps, files and backups (§5.1).
API The list of questions a program answers, and how to ask them. /api/* paths on the server (§3.4).
App Group A shared folder that an iPhone app and its helpers can all use. group.app.branchchat.ios (§6.1).
APNs Apple's service for waking iPhones with notifications. Used by web/apnspush.py (§3.9).
Backup A copy kept somewhere safe in case the original is lost. Server backups: §7.11. Not the same as the key backup.
bash / fish Two kinds of shell: the program in a terminal that reads your commands. Server commands are bash.
Blob A big lump of data, such as a photo or video. A locked, uploaded file, stored in 8 MiB pieces under blobs/ (§3.8).
Bridge A guarded doorway between the web page and the phone or desktop app around it. BranchChatNative / TwigumNative, bcDesktopApp (§4.9).
Cache A nearby copy kept so things load faster. The service worker's caches and the bc-history message cache (§4.3, §4.7).
Certificate (TLS) A digital ID card that proves a website is who it says it is, so the padlock shows. Provided by Cloudflare, Caddy or your proxy (§7.4).
Chat key The private key a device uses to open the wraps meant for it (the key to its letterbox). ECDH P-256 key pair (§5.2).
Ciphertext Locked (scrambled) text. What the server stores instead of messages.
cid A label the app puts on each send, so a double tap doesn't send twice. De-duplicated for 600 s (§3.4.6).
ck The key for one Lobby message, handed to a public-mode server so it can check for bad words. §5.8.
Cloudflare Tunnel A private pipe from your server out to Cloudflare, so people can reach it without opening your router. Access mode tunnel (§7.4).
Config / configuration Settings. config.env plus environment variables (§3.11, Appendix B).
Container / Docker A sealed box with a program and everything it needs, that runs the same anywhere. server/docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile (§7.7).
Cookie A small note a website asks your browser to keep and show again next time. huzz_chat_session (sign-in) and huzz_chat_verified (this browser passed the email code) (§3.6).
Counter (ctr) A number that goes up with every message a device sends, so an old message can't be sent again. Part of the signature and AAD; server refuses reuse (ctr_reused) (§5.4).
Cross-sign One of your devices vouching for another of your devices. twigum-device-cross-v1 (§5.3).
CSRF A trick where another website makes your signed-in browser do something without you knowing. Blocked by the request guard (§3.2, §3.12).
CSP A rule sheet that tells the browser which code and pictures a page may load. §3.12.
cv The server's "something changed" number. Used by /api/wait (§3.5).
Deploy Putting a new version onto a server. install.sh update (§7.10).
Device One phone, computer or browser where you use Twigum, with its own keys. Max 8 per account (§3.7).
Directory The public list of servers that chose to be listed. On the front door; servers report with BC_DIRECTORY_REPORT=1 (§3.14).
DNS The internet's phone book: turns names into addresses.
Domain name A web address name you rent, like example.com.
ECDH / ECDSA Maths for public-key locks (ECDH: two keys agree a shared secret; ECDSA: signatures). P-256 curve (§5.1).
Encryption Scrambling information so only someone with the key can read it. §5.
End-to-end encryption Locking that happens on the sender's device and is only undone on the recipient's, so the middle (the server) can't read it. True for DMs, groups and files, with the exceptions in §5.8.
Environment variable A setting handed to a program when it starts, outside any file. Wins over config.env (§3.11).
Epoch One "generation" of a group's shared key; a new one starts when people join or leave. §5.4.
Extension (iOS) A small helper that belongs to an iPhone app. Notification Service and Share extensions (§6.1).
Fingerprint A short code made from a key, used to check it is the right one. Device fingerprints (§5.1), server key fingerprint k= (§3.14).
Front door The public starting page where you pick your server; also hosts the directory. https://twigum.app (BC_HOME_MODE=1) (§1.3, §3.14).
Git / repository / commit / SHA Git keeps every version of the code; the repository is the whole collection; a commit is one saved change; its SHA is its unique 40-character name. This guide describes commit 2da30e8f.
Hash A one-way fingerprint of some data; you can't get the data back from it. Passwords (scrypt), invite tokens and login codes are stored hashed.
Health check A tiny question that proves a server is up. /healthz, /api/health (§3.2).
HKDF / PBKDF2 Ways to turn a secret into a proper key; PBKDF2 is deliberately slow to stop password guessing. §5.1, §5.6.
Home / home mode A server that acts as the front door and directory. BC_HOME_MODE=1.
Host / hostname A computer's name on the network, like chat.example.com. Checked against BC_PUBLIC_URL and BC_HOSTS (§3.2).
HSTS A note telling browsers "always use the secure (https) address for me". §3.12.
HTTP / HTTPS The language browsers and servers speak; HTTPS is the private, locked version. HTTPS is required (§7.1).
IndexedDB A small database inside your browser. Keeps device keys and the locked message cache (§4.3).
Invite / invite token A one-time ticket to join a server. 256-bit, single use, 72 hours (§3.6, §3.14).
JSON A simple text format for data, with {"name": "value"} pairs. All API answers.
Key / key pair Secret data that locks or unlocks. A key pair has a public half (safe to share) and a private half (never shared). §5.
Key backup A locked copy of your keys kept on the server so a new device can read old messages. v2, opened only with your recovery key or backup passphrase (§5.6).
Key pin / TOFU Remembering a friend's device seal the first time you see it ("trust on first use"), and warning if it ever changes. IndexedDB device-pins on each device (§5.3). Not the same as pinned messages.
Keychain / Keystore The phone's locked safe for passwords and keys (iPhone: Keychain; Android: Keystore). §6.1.1, §6.2.
Lobby A server-wide public room. On public-mode servers the server can read Lobby posts (§5.8).
Log The server's diary of what happened, mostly errors. No request lines are logged (§3.13).
Long-polling Asking "anything new?" and having the server wait to answer until there is. /api/wait (§3.5).
Megolm / Olm / vodozemac A newer way of locking group chats, and the library that does it. Off by default (BC_VODOZEMAC) (§5.5).
Migration Converting stored data to a newer format. migrate_state, manage.py migrate (§3.2).
Native app An app built for one kind of device (iPhone, Android, desktop), not just a web page. Thin wrappers round the web app (§6).
Port A numbered door on a computer that a program listens at. Twigum: 8766 on the server; people use 443 (HTTPS).
Public mode Extra features for an open, public server: sign-up, bad-word filter, reports. PUBLIC_MODE (docs/public-mode.md).
Push A way to wake a sleeping phone or browser when something arrives. Web Push and APNs; Android uses its own background check (§3.9).
PWA A website you can install like an app. manifest.webmanifest, sw.js.
QR code A square barcode a camera can read. Invite links can be shown as QR codes.
Rate limit A speed limit on how often something can be done. e.g. 1 message per second; invite limits (Appendix B).
Recovery key Your personal 56-character code that opens your key backup. Keep it safe; nobody else can recover it. §5.6.
Reverse proxy A program in front of the server that handles HTTPS and passes requests on. Caddy, nginx, Traefik, Cloudflare (§7.4).
Rollback Putting the previous version back. install.sh update rolls back by itself (§7.10).
SAS A short code and emoji shown on two devices; if they match, nobody is listening in the middle. Device approval and device linking (§5.3, §5.5).
scrypt A slow, one-way password scrambler. Password hashes (§3.6).
Service worker A helper script the browser keeps for the app: offline copy, notifications, updates. web/sw.js (§4.7).
Session Being signed in. A signed cookie plus a row in sessions.json, 30 days by default (§3.6).
SHELL_V / BC_ASSET The app's version "stamp" for its cached files. Changes every release (§4.7).
Signature / signing key A digital wax seal only one device can make and anyone can check. ECDSA P-256, can't be copied out of the device (§5.2).
Signing outage 9–11 Nov 2026, when some messages were sent without seals. Special label in §5.3.
SMTP The standard way servers send email. §7.5.
State directory (STATE_DIR) The one folder where the server keeps everything. §3.3.
sudo "Do this as the computer's administrator."
Sync Fetching what changed since last time. /api/sync (§3.5).
systemd / service / journal Linux's program-starter, the programs it runs, and its log. Service branch-chat.
Terminal A window where you type commands.
Tombstone A marker left where something was deleted, so others can see it's gone. Deleted messages; used invites (14 days).
TOTP / two-factor A 6-digit code from an authenticator app that changes every 30 seconds, as a second lock on your account. §3.6.
Turnstile Cloudflare's "are you human?" check. Public sign-up (§3.11).
Twigum The app. Formerly BranchChat; code name huzz-chat. Use only "Twigum" in anything people read. Identifiers such as the iOS bundle ID app.branchchat.ios, its App Group group.app.branchchat.ios, the APNs topic, and storage/crypto IDs (huzz-chat IndexedDB, huzz_chat_session, branchchat-backup:v2, branchchat-safety-v1, huzz-chat-salt-v1, keychain service app.branchchat.dev.ios.servers) stay as they are on purpose: renaming them would break updates, keychains and decryption. Canonical link: twigum.app.
VAPID The key that identifies your server to browser push services. vapid.json (§3.9).
Version / build number Which release this is. YY.MM.DDRR and YYYYMMDDRR (Start here).
WebCrypto The cryptography toolkit built into every modern browser. web/static/crypto.js.
WebView A browser window built into an app. iOS WKWebView, Android WebView, Electron (§6).
Wrap A copy of a message's key, locked for one device. §5.1, §5.4.

Appendix B. Every setting

🌱In plain words

This is the full list of settings the server reads. You only ever need a handful (§3.11 lists the important ones); the rest have sensible defaults. "Environment only" means the setting must be given when the program starts (for example in the systemd unit or Docker's environment:), because the server ignores it in config.env.

Configuration variables read by the server code at this commit: the 142 BC_*/APNS_*/PUBLIC_MODE names found in the first pass, plus the TURNSTILE_* primary names added after review. This is not the full set: these legacy aliases are also read: BRANCH_OWNER (bcconfig.py:231), OPEN_SIGNUP, LANGUAGE_FILTER, REPORT_BLOCK, FULL_ACCOUNT_DELETE, LOGIN_LIMITS, LOBBY_LINK_FILTER, LANGUAGE_LOCK, HOST_LINK (publicmode.py:63-78). "Default" is the value in code or the Administrator-page schema; secret values are never shown. Labels come from web/adminpage.py SCHEMA where the variable is editable there. "First read at" is where the code reads the value; for schema settings that are not listed with a reader, it is the schema row. "(environment only)" means config.env and the Administrator page have no effect (§3.11).

Appendix C. Known limitations and things to check

Topic What to know
Download links Server packages are pinned to https://github.com/NexusMcNexis/twigum-releases/releases/tag/server-v26.11.1401 (not /releases/latest, which the app updaters use). Use the twigum-server-* names; the versioned branch-chat-server-26.11.1401-* files are the same. The git repository is private; public source installs use the source package on that release (§7.2).
docs/DIRECTORY.md Matches the code described in §3.14 (default home https://twigum.app; invites go through the home except three cases). https://branchchat.app stays a valid home and does not redirect.
Encryption claims docs/self-hosting.md says the server "cannot read messages or files". That is true for direct messages, groups and files, but not for the Lobby on public-mode servers, accounts with an old (v1) key backup, or a server that serves modified app code (§5.8).
Fedora/RHEL, Docker Desktop Described in docs/server/ but not yet tested on real machines.
.deb/.rpm packages "Coming soon" (docs/server/deb-rpm.md); branch-chat-setup exists only with those packages.
macOS desktop app npm run dist:mac is configured but has never been built or tested (desktop/BUILD.md:30-32).
Version tools tools/bcversion.py writes the month and the day without a leading zero (26.1.…, 26.11.101); the version rule is two digits (26.01.0101).
Stale comments Some comments and READMEs disagree with the code (session length, password minimum, desktop profile path). The code's values are the ones in this guide: sessions 30 days, passwords 12 characters.
Periodic clean-up Unfinished uploads are removed only when the server starts (§3.2); there is no timer. A restart (every update does one) cleans up.
No 96-hour file expiry Shared files are kept until the message is deleted; only videos are removed when space runs short (§3.3).
